jobs.description:
About the Position

The Designer II is an entry-level contributor focused on strengthening discipline knowledge, advancing modeling capability, and taking greater ownership of coordination and documentation across projects. You’ll apply workflows, tools, and BIM standards with increasing independence while supporting engineers and project teams in delivering coordinated construction documents.
You’ll contribute to project delivery through modeling, drawing updates, coordination support, documentation, and early QA activities. As your technical understanding grows, you’ll take on more complex coordination and documentation responsibilities across Telecom/ICT, Audiovisual, Security, Acoustics, Network, Wi-Fi, and other technology disciplines as applicable.
Working closely with engineering mentors, production staff, and project teams, you’ll help maintain model quality, support coordination efforts, and reinforce TEECOM’s BIM and documentation standards. You’ll begin identifying coordination risks, improving model organization, and contributing to more efficient project workflows.
This position reflects growing technical confidence, increased independence, and consistent application of TEECOM’s modeling, coordination, and documentation standards.

Developing Technical Execution and Coordination

  • As a Designer II, your impact comes from growing independence, increasing coordination awareness, and your ability to maintain model health and documentation quality. You contribute in three key ways:

    • Learn From Mentors and Project Teams

  • You build independence by taking on modeling, documentation, and early coordination work with moderate supervision.
  • You strengthen project delivery by preparing work that anticipates next steps for production and engineering teams.
  • You improve coordination quality by working with cross-discipline teams to resolve straightforward modeling issues.
  • You grow your BIM capability by developing proficiency in clash detection, model aggregation, and review workflows in Navisworks or ACC.
    • Contribute to Team Learning and Collaboration
  • You build your skills and support team learning through structured training journeys, mentorship, and hands-on project experience.
  • You help improve team processes by sharing lessons learned, asking questions, and offering feedback that enhances documentation and standards.
  • You support consistency and quality by updating standards, notes, and documentation—while beginning to help guide Designer I team members.
  • You elevate team performance by contributing to discussions on project challenges, coordination risks, and opportunities to improve production workflows.

    • Improve the TEECOM System

  • You reinforce consistency and clarity across projects by applying TEECOM’s production and BIM standards—including naming conventions, linking practices, view templates, worksets, and model organization.
  • You support coordinated delivery by maintaining accurate, well-organized models, markups, notes, and documentation with minimal rework.
  • You enhance quality by identifying issues in models, drawings, or workflows early and raising them proactively to senior staff.
  • You help evolve TEECOM’s system by offering thoughtful suggestions to improve production templates, views, families, and modeling workflows.

What Success in this Position Looks Like

  • You produce accurate, coordinated Revit models, drawings, and documentation with minimal rework.
  • You complete most production tasks independently and clarify direction early.
  • You support engineers by preparing design calculations, specifications, product research, and coordinating documentation.
  • You manage your task load effectively—updating Asana, communicating risks early, and meeting deadlines across multiple projects.
  • You maintain a healthy model structure by managing links, worksets, view templates, and model organization in alignment with TEECOM’s BIM standards.
  • You apply TEECOM standards consistently and help identify gaps or opportunities for improvement.
  • You participate in meetings and prepare clear, organized notes that support team alignment.
  • You collaborate with production and engineers to resolve coordination issues and strengthen deliverable quality.
  • You maintain accurate documentation in GitHub and begin contributing basic Pull Requests with guidance.
  • You meet utilization targets and complete daily time and expense entries accurately.
  • You model TEECOM’s Core Values—Care, Trust, and Value—through communication, teamwork, and reliable execution.

Responsibilities and Expectations

  • These responsibilities and expectations represent what is required to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.

    • Annual and Quarterly

  • Strengthen discipline knowledge through hands-on project experience, applying feedback to build technical judgment and increasing independence.
  • Participate in performance assessments and apply feedback to improve modeling accuracy, coordination awareness, and delivery consistency.
  • Complete required training journeys and continue building discipline specialization while supporting cross-discipline collaboration.
  • Maintain organized, accurate models, documentation, and design updates that reflect current project intent with reduced oversight.
  • Contribute to discipline documentation improvements by identifying gaps, sharing lessons learned, and supporting updates in GitHub.

    • Monthly and Biweekly

  • Deliver accurate, coordinated modeling, documentation, and production work with increasing independence and reduced oversight.
  • Prepare and update Revit models, sheets, narratives, and calculations aligned with project standards and technical guidance.
  • Support coordination by incorporating redlines, resolving straightforward modeling issues, and identifying basic conflicts across disciplines.
  • Participate in discipline, project, and engineering meetings, contributing updates, coordination input, and organized documentation when assigned.
  • Apply BIM standards by maintaining model health, organization, and consistency across views, links, and templates.
  • Support early QA efforts by reviewing work for accuracy, clarity, and adherence to TEECOM workflows.
  • Document design decisions, coordination updates, and project changes within TEECOM tools to support team visibility.
  • Maintain accurate and timely time and expense entries to support delivery accountability.

    • Weekly and Daily

  • Contribute to coordinated project delivery by updating models, drawings, calculations, and documentation with increasing independence.
  • Participate in project meetings, coordination sessions, and daily huddles, clearly communicating status, risks, and design questions.
  • Implement markups, modeling updates, calculations, and delegated tasks while maintaining organized files and documentation.
  • Maintain accurate task tracking and design updates across TEECOM tools to support team visibility and delivery alignment.
  • Coordinate with cross-discipline teams to resolve straightforward modeling or documentation issues identified during coordination or BIM reviews.
  • Apply TEECOM standards and workflows by documenting design decisions, standards clarifications, and client-specific requirements when appropriate.
  • Participate in basic QA and clash detection workflows, identifying conflicts and supporting model coordination efforts.
  • Ask clarifying questions early, confirm assumptions, and apply feedback to strengthen technical execution and modeling accuracy.
  • Maintain accurate daily time and expense entries and communicate promptly with project teams to support delivery momentum.

    • As Needed

  • Support site visits or existing conditions verification with minimal oversight and clearly document findings.
  • Review models and drawings from other disciplines, identify coordination issues, and escalate risks when needed.
  • Support contractor submittal reviews under the supervision of senior team members.
  • Prepare diagrams, schedules, or documentation for internal or client deliverables with increasing independence.
  • Perform targeted research, gather product data, and support early specification or design development efforts.
  • Update or refine templates, views, tools, or workflows and suggest practical improvements where appropriate.
  • Assist with Navisworks or ACC coordination workflows, including preparing views, exports, or basic clash review support.

Supervisory / Mentorship / Training Responsibilities

  • Supervisory: None. Designer II roles focus on developing stronger judgment, coordination skills, and production independence while supporting senior team members.
  • Mentorship: Provide informal guidance to Designer I team members by answering questions, sharing modeling approaches, and helping clarify workflows—always aligned with direction from senior engineers. Seek and apply feedback from your Mentor and project leaders to continue building discipline expertise.
  • Training: Actively participate in structured training journeys, mentorship, and hands-on learning to strengthen discipline fundamentals.

Experience and Qualifications

  • Education: BS in Engineering (Electrical preferred), Architecture, or a related field; or equivalent experience.
  • Experience: 2+ years of experience in the AEC industry with demonstrated proficiency in Revit modeling, drafting, and construction documentation, including coordination or field exposure supporting construction or site activities.
  • Preferred: Experience supporting technology system design (Telecom/ICT, Audiovisual, Security, Acoustics, Network, Wi-Fi, and other technology disciplines) and familiarity with coordinated drawing sets.
  • Experience maintaining Revit model structure, including links, worksets, view templates, and model organization.
  • Familiarity with basic clash detection workflows in Navisworks or Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC).
  • Ability to produce accurate models and drawings with minimal rework, follow established workflows, and incorporate feedback efficiently.
  • Strong organizational, communication, and coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and support project delivery across several projects.
  • Growing knowledge of technology systems and basic engineering principles; ability to perform introductory calculations, research, or product evaluations with guidance.
  • Proficiency in Autodesk Revit and/or AutoCAD; working knowledge of Bluebeam Studio, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Asana, and GitHub.
    • Industry certifications preferred but not required:
  • EIT — plus
  • CDT — plus
  • Introductory Revit/BIM/drafting certifications — plus

Physical Demands

  • These physical demands represent what is required to perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations will be provided as needed.
  • Prolonged desk work using a computer, keyboard, mouse, and telephone.
  • Regular reading, writing, and communication in virtual and in-person settings.
  • Occasional travel to client sites for meetings, surveys, or inspections.
  • Site walks may require standing or walking for extended periods, climbing stairs, and navigating construction or utility areas.
  • Field activities may involve bending, kneeling, or maneuvering in confined spaces.
  • May occasionally lift or move equipment weighing up to 25 pounds.

Work Environment

  • These work environment characteristics represent the conditions encountered while performing essential job functions. Reasonable accommodations will be provided as needed.
  • Approximately 75% of work is performed in a remote or office environment using standard office equipment.
  • Approximately 25% occurs at client sites, including construction environments and existing facilities.
  • Construction sites may include exposure to elevated noise levels, dust, uneven or unfinished walking surfaces, variable lighting conditions, and active construction operations.
  • Utility rooms and similar spaces may have restricted access or may not fully comply with ADA accessibility standards. When access limitations exist, TEECOM will support coordinating reasonable accommodations with site-controlling contractor or alternative means to perform essential job functions.
  • All accidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions must be reported immediately to the site superintendent and internally to People Operations.
Your level will be evaluated and determined during the interview process.
We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas.

In the absence of a signed Recruitment Fee Agreement, TEECOM will not consider or agree to payment of any referral compensation or recruiter fee. In the event a recruiter or agency submits a resume or candidate without a previously signed agreement, TEECOM explicitly reserves the right to pursue and hire those candidate(s) without any financial obligation to the recruiter or agency. Any unsolicited resumes, including those submitted to hiring managers, are deemed to be the property of TEECOM.

jobs.title: 2014 Senior Embedded Software Engineer - Test OS
jobs.excerpt: Senior Embedded Software Engineer (SP1 - RVT): ¿Qué es?
jobs.description:
Senior Embedded Software Engineer (SP1 - RVT):

¿Qué es?

Es un profesional especializado en el desarrollo, integración y adaptación de sistemas operativos embebidos (como Embedded Linux o RTOS) para ECUs (Unidades de Control Electrónico), con enfoque en la replicación y optimización de un Test OS en plataformas automotrices.

¿Cómo lo hace?

Analiza y porta el Test OS (usado para pruebas, diagnósticos y validación) de vehículos Gen2 a Gen1, adaptando su arquitectura, servicios y flujo de despliegue.

Desarrolla capas de abstracción de software para garantizar la compatibilidad entre el Test OS y el hardware de las ECUs.

Integra funcionalidades clave como diagnósticos (UDS, DoIP), flasheo de firmware, adquisición de datos (logging) y monitoreo de salud en tiempo real.

Automatiza pruebas (SIL, HIL y a nivel vehicular) para validar el comportamiento de las ECUs y los componentes conectados.

Depura problemas entre capas (software, hardware, comunicación) y colabora con equipos multidisciplinarios para cerrar brechas de plataforma.

¿Por qué es crucial?

Su trabajo asegura que los sistemas embebidos en vehículos Gen1 funcionen con la misma robustez y capacidad de prueba que los de Gen2, garantizando calidad, seguridad y cumplimiento de estándares automotrices (ej: ASPICE, MISRA C).

Requirements

Habilidades:

Lenguajes: C (avanzado +5 años), C++ (intermedio/avanzado 3-5+ años), Python (intermedio 2-5 años), Bash (intermedio 2-5 años).

Sistemas operativos embebidos: Embedded Linux (avanzado +5 años), RTOS (avanzado +5 años).

Protocolos de comunicación: CAN, CAN FD, UDS (avanzado +5 años), DoIP, Automotive Ethernet (intermedio 2-5 años).

Herramientas: Vector CANoe/CANalyzer/CANape (avanzado +5 años), GDB, JTAG (intermedio/avanzado 3-5+ años).

Pruebas automatizadas: GoogleTest, pytest (intermedio/avanzado 3-5+ años), SIL, HIL (avanzado +5 años).

CI/CD y control de versiones: Git (avanzado +5 años), Jenkins, GitLab CI (intermedio/avanzado 3-5+ años).

Firmware para ECUs: Integración, flasheo, diagnósticos (DIDs, DTCs) (avanzado +5 años).

Estándares: ASPICE, MISRA C (avanzado +5 años).

Visa (Obligatorio) - Viajaran a USA por el equipo de cliente

Actividades del puesto:

Análisis y adaptación del Test OS:

Analizar la arquitectura, servicios y flujo de despliegue del Test OS implementado en vehículos Gen2.

Portar el Test OS a las ECUs Gen1 de RVT, asegurando compatibilidad con el hardware existente.

Desarrollo de software embebido:

Desarrollar capas de abstracción de plataforma para facilitar la comunicación, control y monitoreo de las ECUs.

Implementar módulos de software para integración de diagnósticos, flasheo de firmware y adquisición de datos.

Integración de funcionalidades clave:

Integrar diagnósticos de ECU (DIDs, DTCs) usando protocolos como UDS y DoIP.

Implementar rutinas de flasheo de firmware para actualizaciones seguras en las ECUs.

Configurar sistemas de logging y monitoreo de salud para registrar y analizar datos en tiempo real.

Automatización de pruebas:

Diseñar y desarrollar pruebas SIL (Software-in-the-Loop) para validar el software en entornos simulados.

Crear pruebas HIL (Hardware-in-the-Loop) para validar el software en conjunto con hardware real.

Implementar pruebas a nivel vehicular para validar el comportamiento del sistema en condiciones reales.

Depuración y resolución de problemas:

Depurar problemas entre capas (software, hardware, comunicación) en las ECUs.

Colaborar con equipos de ECU, eléctrica, sistemas, validación y hardware para identificar y resolver brechas de plataforma.

Colaboración y documentación:

Trabajar con equipos multidisciplinarios para asegurar la integración y validación del Test OS en Gen1.

Documentar procesos, cambios y resultados de las pruebas y adaptaciones realizadas.

Cumplimiento de estándares:

Asegurar que el desarrollo del software cumpla con estándares como ASPICE y MISRA C.

Validar que las soluciones implementadas cumplan con los requisitos de seguridad y calidad del cliente.

In 2026, Action1 was recognized as the fastest-growing founder-led cybersecurity company in America on the Inc. 5000. We are looking for a Dev Manager to lead the engineering team responsible for integrations between our product and external systems, including the Integrations Store.   • Improve integration reliability, performance, and observability, and guide the team in resolving production issues.
  • Coordinate with other engineering teams and external partners to manage dependencies and compatibility.

Requirements

  • Experience with secure authentication and authorization for integrations.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to align engineering work with product priorities.
  • Professional working proficiency in English for leading an English-speaking team and collaborating across functions.

Nice to have:

  • Experience writing automated integration and contract tests.

Benefits

jobs.title: Senior QA Engineer Performance & Scalability
jobs.excerpt: We're looking for a Senior QA Engineer, Performance & Scalability who doesn't wait to be told what to test.
jobs.description:
We're looking for a Senior QA Engineer, Performance & Scalability who doesn't wait to be told what to test. You'll own performance and scalability across our platform, 30+ microservices, event-driven flows, and the legacy dependencies that come with a real production system at scale. This isn't a "run a load test before release" role. This is a role where you make performance a first-class concern from day one, where you define the thresholds that decide pass or fail, and where you hold the bar when something is degrading and nobody yet knows why.

You'll be the performance voice in every room you walk into, design discussions, architecture reviews, incident retrospectives. When latency spikes, you're already halfway through the trace. When a new service is being scoped, performance is already in the delivery plan because you put it there.

What you can expect to be doing:

  • Own Performance from Day One - You embed performance thinking into the delivery plan before code is written, not as an afterthought before release. You make performance testing a natural part of how teams build and ship — not a gate they hit at the end.

  • Define What Good Looks Like - You own the thresholds, metrics, and SLOs that govern pass or fail. You decide what a breach means, you set the budgets (latency, error rate, throughput), and you make those signals objective enough that a pipeline can act on them without a human reading graphs.

  • Test Services in Isolation, at Production Scale - You design and build performance tests for individual services, stubbing downstream and third-party dependencies so each journey is tested on its own merits. You map load to real production traffic to find where things bend and where they break.

  • Lead Performance in CI - You integrate performance testing into CI/CD so regressions are caught automatically, early, and fast. You own the fail-fast signals and keep them trustworthy.

  • Build Reusable, Scalable Assets - You build performance tests as code, reusable components, templates, and utilities that scale across teams and services. You handle data seeding and test setup so runs are repeatable and realistic.

  • Diagnose, Don't Just Report - You root-cause regressions across the stack, reading logs and tracing requests through distributed systems to find the source yourself rather than waiting for someone to hand it to you.

  • Reach Out and Drive Outcomes - You engage the right stakeholders, engineering, platform, product - to turn findings into fixes. You don't file a report and walk away; you drive the outcome.

  • Influence Decisions - You raise performance and scalability risks early, challenge assumptions constructively, and bring people with you. When a design won't scale, you say so before it ships.

What we’re looking for:

  • 5+ years in performance engineering, with a track record of owning performance across complex, modern systems, not just executing someone else's load test.

  • Deep performance testing expertise. Hands-on experience designing realistic load models, running load, stress, soak and spike tests, and interpreting results meaningfully.

  • K6 or similar - You have real, hands-on depth with k6 for building and running performance tests.

  • Monitoring and observability know-how. You're comfortable with tools like Datadog, Grafana, CloudWatch or similar, and you use them proactively to correlate test results with what the system is actually doing, not just when something is already on fire.

  • Strong programming ability. You're extremely strong in at least one language. We use TypeScript across our stack; if your fundamentals are solid in another language, we're confident you'll pick it up fast.

  • Microservices and distributed systems. You understand service-oriented architectures, dependencies, and the realities of testing a service in isolation — stubbing, mocking, contract boundaries, as well as end-to-end.

  • CI/CD fluency - You've integrated performance testing into CI/CD pipelines and understand how to keep feedback fast and signals reliable. Experience with AWS infrastructure is strongly preferred.

  • Strong communication and presence. You participate fully in agile ceremonies and cross-team conversations. You don't sit quietly when something needs to be said

Nice to Have

  • Experience in fintech, wealth management, or regulated financial services.

  • Experience using AI-assisted tooling to accelerate performance work.

  • Contributions to internal quality guilds, communities of practice, or engineering culture initiatives.

  • Experience mentoring engineers on performance and testing best practices.

What we’re really looking for: ✍️

Beyond the skills and the experience, we want someone who operates with ownership and independence. You don't wait for permission to improve something. You see a gap in coverage, a flaky test, a missing dashboard — and you fix it. You treat the Wealth Management experience line as yours, and you hold yourself to the same standard you hold the product to.

You're not a gatekeeper. You're a quality enabler. And you make every team you work with better at shipping reliable software.

Interested? We'd love to hear from you. Apply and tell us about a time you changed how quality worked on a team, not just what you tested, but how you made testing better for everyone around you.

⏰ Working Hours ⏰

  • Monday to Thursday: 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM

  • Friday: 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM (Start your weekend early!)

Enjoy a structured yet balanced workweek, with an early Friday finish to kickstart your weekend!

PERKS🎁

  • £60,000 - £70,000 per annum

  • Discretionary Performance-Related Annual Bonus

  • Workplace pension scheme - We invest in your future with a workplace pension scheme, contributing 5% on earnings up to £50,000. Plan ahead with confidence while you grow your career! 🚀

  • Private medical insurance (medical history disregarded)

  • Opportunity to have a huge impact on our product while fast-tracking your knowledge, responsibility and skills in a high-growth fintech startup 🚀

Our Interview Process: 📖

About Chip

Chip’s mission is to make your life wealthy

We're building the wealth super app of the future. An app to build your long-term wealth across savings, investments and pensions.

We use technology to break down barriers so users can invest like the ultra-wealthy, giving them one simple place to manage, grow and protect their wealth.

The Sunday Times listed Chip as the 6th fastest growing tech company in Britain… and we're not slowing down. Chip serves over 400,000 active customers and looks after over £6billion in assets. These customers trust us to build the most amazing product we can, so working at Chip comes with real purpose.

NeoWork is a premium nearshoring and offshoring partner that builds and manages high-performance dedicated teams for North American clients. We specialize in providing the operational backbone for fast-growing companies, ensuring that their critical processes—from lead intake to client delivery—are handled with precision and speed. We are currently seeking an Operations Manager to lead a mission-critical intake team for one of our key legal and healthcare partners.

As an Operations Manager (Client Delivery), you are the primary operational owner for a dedicated intake team. In our nearshoring model, you serve as the vital bridge between NeoWork’s delivery team in Latin America/the Philippines and the client’s leadership in the United States. You are responsible for the overall performance, quality assurance, and execution of the account.

This is a high-accountability role. You will spend your day managing real-time call volumes, auditing intake files for accuracy before they reach the client, and using Advanced Excel to analyze performance trends. You are responsible for ensuring your team hits "lightning-fast" response times (Target: within minutes) while maintaining the meticulous quality standards our clients expect from a premium offshore partner.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Client Liaison & Delivery: Act as the main point of contact for the client’s leadership. You own the daily operational relationship and ensure NeoWork’s delivery aligns perfectly with the client's strategic goals.
  • SLA & Performance Oversight: Manage a high-volume intake floor. You must ensure 100% compliance with strict responsiveness targets and rapid lead follow-up.
  • QA & Audit Framework: Design and manage the QA systems. You will personally review completed intakes to identify gaps and resolve errors before they reach the client’s legal or processing teams.
  • Analytical Reporting: You will live in Excel. You’ll track KPIs like call volume, conversion rates, and agent efficiency, transforming raw data into sophisticated dashboards for client stakeholders.
  • Team & System Administration: Oversee the team’s use of CRM platforms, dialers, and VDI client systems. You manage the scheduling, attendance, and continuous coaching of your dedicated unit.
  • Process Optimization: Constantly "stress-test" the current workflow to identify bottlenecks and scale operations as the client account grows.

Requirements

  • Experience: 4–7+ years in Operations, Call Center Management, or Intake Management.
  • Leadership: Proven experience leading high-performance teams in a high-volume, performance-driven environment.
  • Technical Mastery:Advanced Excel skills are mandatory. You must be able to build reports, use pivot tables/formulas, and create dashboards. Proficiency with CRM and Telephony tools is required.
  • Client Management: Strong stakeholder management skills; you must be able to confidently present performance data and strategy to US-based client leadership in English.
  • Background (Preferred): Specific experience in Legal, Healthcare, or Sales-driven intake is a significant advantage.
  • Mindset: A high-ownership "operator" mentality with meticulous attention to detail. You are someone who catches the errors that everyone else misses.

Success Metrics (KPIs)

  • SLA Adherence: Consistently hitting the "minutes-to-respond" target for all inbound leads.
  • QA Accuracy: Reducing the error rate of files sent to the client to <2%.

  • Reporting: Delivery of a weekly automated performance dashboard that provides the client with clear visibility into team ROI.

This team is building an AI-native operating model for service delivery — agentic systems that reason about the next best action, and durable workflow infrastructure that carries those decisions out reliably.

About the role

The Principal Product Manager, Directed Workflows drives the vision, strategy, and execution for how ZHL's sales and service process gets encoded as directed work. AI agents reason over each customer's situation, adapt that process to the specific opportunity in front of them, and determine the next work that should happen: the action, the outcome it is meant to create, the quality bar it must meet, and the skills required to execute it. You will own that loop across engagement and loan production. You design the AI harness (context, tools, memory, orchestration, escalation, guardrails) that determines what those agents reason over and what work they produce. You own the eval infrastructure that scores those decisions against the process you defined, learns from operator feedback, and uses experiments to decide what to keep, change, or retire.

jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Power Digital is an AI-Native Growth Firm built at the intersection of world-class talent and proprietary technology. We help leading and emerging brands grow by combining deep vertical expertise, strategic thinking, and enterprise intelligence to drive measurable business outcomes.

For more than a decade, we have built our business around one belief: the best technology makes great people better. Our teams of strategists, creatives, analysts, and technologists use Omega, our AI operating system, to surface opportunities faster, investigate what is driving performance, and execute approved work with greater speed and precision. Behind Omega is Iris, our proprietary intelligence layer, built on years of real performance data, strategic frameworks, testing, and learnings from across our client portfolio. AI expands the capacity of our people to think, create, solve harder problems, and make better decisions. Human judgment, creativity, and accountability remain central to how we work.

As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. We partner closely with our clients as an extension of their teams, working across strategy, execution, and measurement to identify what is truly blocking growth and determine what to do next. Our culture is built on people who are curious, ambitious, accountable, and committed to delivering meaningful results for our clients and for one another.

At Power Digital, we believe the future belongs to teams that combine the best talent with the best technology. We are building that future today.

**We support 100% remote, in-office, or hybrid work styles for anyone legally eligible to work in the U.S.

A day in the life:

As the VP of Strategy, their days are spent embedded inside the Division's book of business, where strategy meets performance. They might start by reviewing which clients are pacing below goal in Omega, join a Group Director to reset strategy on an at-risk Top 15 account, pressure-test a QBR narrative before it goes to a client's C-suite, and close with office hours helping Account Directors build a cross-channel growth plan. Across all of it, they spot common problems and strategic gaps and turn them into solutions, playbooks, and trainings that raise the floor for the whole Division. They serve as the Division's senior strategy and performance lead. While Group Directors own the client relationships and the book, the VP of Strategy ensures the strategy behind every client is sharp enough to hit goals, retain business, and drive expansion.

The VP of Strategy is the senior strategy and performance leader embedded directly within a vertical CX Division. The role is an evolution of the VP/MD of Strategic Solutions, moving strategy out of a central unit and into the Division it serves. It functions as a coaching and expert resource rather than a traditional management layer: ADs report directly to GDs, while the VP of Strategy is deployed across the book where strategic rigor and performance matter most. Depending on the scale and needs of the division, the VP of Strategy may manage a small pod of strategic leaders and executors. The role centers on four core pillars:

  • Client Performance & Strategy (40%): Owning the strategy and performance standard for the Division's book so clients achieve their goals.
  • Top Client Retention & Escalations (25%): Serving as the strategy and performance lead for the Division's Top 15 clients, as well as supporting at-risk accounts.
  • Omega & Strategic Solutions Enablement (20%): Driving Goals + Composer adoption, the Power Circuit, and playbooks across the Division.
  • AD & GD Strategic Coaching (15%): Raising the strategic capability of the Division's Account Directors and Group Directors.

Ultimately, this role is built on the conviction that clients who hit their goals stay and grow. Better performance serves as the primary retention lever and the foundation for long-term service expansion.

Key Responsibilities:

Client Performance & Strategy (Target 40%):

  • Priority Client Pitch Support: For P1 clients, support in the narrative build and forecasting within the new business pitch process to ensure alignment between client stakeholders, sales, and delivery.
  • Performance Ownership: Own the strategy and performance standard across the Division's book. Track every client against goal (below, at or above) and drive recovery plans for clients below goal.
  • Goals + Composer: Ensure every client has quality goals and full context set up in Composer, and that Omega's recommendations are reviewed and acted on by account teams.
  • Cross-Channel Strategy: Design integrated, data-backed strategies and playbooks that move past single-channel solutions where possible (e.g., New Market Entry, BFCM, Subscription, seasonality planning).
  • Measurement: Partner with measurement and data resources so client goals, attribution and reporting are sound. The Division's Media Planner and AI Lead have a dotted line to this role.
  • Proactive Planning: Bring forward-looking strategy to clients, such as seasonality, competitive shifts and annual planning, before they ask for it.

Proactive Top Client Retention & Escalation Support (Target 25%):

  • Top 15 Strategy Lead: Serve as the strategy and performance lead for the Division's Top 15 and Pareto clients, partnering with the GD and executive sponsor on growth plans and long-range plans.
  • At-Risk Turnarounds: Step in on at-risk and escalated accounts. Diagnose root causes and prescribe clear, actionable remediation plans that account teams can execute.
  • Strategic QBRs: Support quarterly growth planning sessions and QBRs that focus on forward-looking strategy.
  • Clear Operating Boundaries: GDs remain the primary decision-makers on their accounts. Engage quarterly or for specific escalations, with clearly defined roles so clients always know who leads.

Omega & Strategic Solutions Enablement (Target 20%):

  • Omega Adoption: Partner with Division leadership and the Innovation team (Division AI Lead and SVP of Innovation) to hit the Division's Omega goals for Goals + Composer coverage, Co-Pilot clients and internal usage.
  • Power Circuit & Playbooks: Carry forward the Power Circuit and solutions roadmap from the Strategic Solutions framework, tailoring playbooks to the Division's vertical.
  • Service Expansion Inputs: Flag white space where stronger strategy uncovers the need for additional services, and hand those opportunities to the GD and AD to lead the SE conversation.
  • Product Feedback: Feed client and performance learnings back into Omega and the Innovation team’s product roadmap to create custom Agentic solutions for Division clients that make Omega more valuable and sticky to the client portfolio.

AD Strategic Coaching (Target 15%):

  • AD Enablement: Coach ADs on strategy, performance diagnosis and leading strategic client conversations through on the job coaching (shadowing, role playing), office hours and Strategic Planning/QBR dry runs.
  • Training & Certification: Partner with Learning and Development team and Product Heads to identify training leads on AD and strategist certification to elevate the floor and level of sophistication of strategy to lead to better client performance.
  • Best-Practice Sharing: Bring standout strategies and case studies to cross-Division roundtables and the monthly Enterprise summit.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

  • Clients Achieving Goals (primary KPI): % of Division's clients with Goals + Composer are at or above goal.
  • Goals + Composer Coverage: 80% of the Division's clients have goals set up in Composer, with 80% of eligible clients using Omega internally by March 31, 2027.
  • Churn Impact: The Division contributes to company monthly churn under 4%, with zero Pareto churn in the Division's Top 10.
    • Retention Saves: Target of 1 Pareto client save and roughly $50K less churn per month.
  • Playbook Integration: 1 new strategic framework, playbook or solution built and adopted in the Division per quarter.
  • Strategic Presence NPS: 80% approval rate on a quarterly survey of GDs and ADs measuring your involvement, strategy quality and effectiveness in putting the Account Director in the "strategic seat."

Most Important Things (MITs):

  • Clients at Goal: Get the Division's book measured against goal in Omega and move clients below goal back on track.
  • Protect the Top 15: Be the strategy partner on the Division's most important accounts so none churn and every one has a clearly defined strategy to hit performance expectations.
  • Strategic Enablement: Elevate the strategic confidence and capability of ADs through coaching, office hours and usable strategic tools.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Base salary + commission opportunities
  • Robust Medical, Dental, Vision insurance plans with up to 100% employer contribution towards employee monthly premium
  • 401(k) plan - 4% employer contribution matching
  • Unlimited Time Off available on day one
  • Up to 4 hours per quarter for paid Volunteer Time Off (VTO) towards philanthropic endeavors
  • Fully flex work environment: full-remote, in-office, or hybrid
  • A one time $100 USD Work From Home (WFH) stipend automatically added to your first paycheck
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • 12 observed United States national holidays + 2 mental health recharge days per year
  • Unlimited opportunities for growth & leadership within a rapidly growing firm
  • Ongoing employee development programs for personal and professional growth (Hedgehog and Vital 5s)
  • Quarterly awards including prize money and recognition for outstanding performance
  • Opportunities to be involved in company DEI initiatives

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, and backgrounds, who strive to make an impact inside and outside of the workplace. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. jobs.title: AI Solutions Engineer - Agents & Automation
jobs.excerpt: About Us HeadQuarters is a global start-up that partners with US cannabis companies to provide support in finance, sales operations, and logistics.
jobs.description:
About Us
HeadQuarters is a global start-up that partners with US cannabis companies to provide support in finance, sales operations, and logistics. We are currently seeking an AI Solutions Engineer to join our growing product development team.

The Role

We're hiring an engineer to design and build AI agents and automations for our external customers in the fast growing Cannabis / CPG industry. You'll partner with our team from the first conversation through delivery: understanding a customer's workflows, scoping what an agent should own, building it on top of their systems, and making sure it runs reliably in production.The most important part of this job is learning how a customer's work actually gets done: sitting with their frontline staff, earning their trust, and turning unwritten rules and exceptions into logic a system can follow.

Once an agent is live, you'll hand it off to one of our Operations Managers, who oversee the agent's day-to-day work and output on the customer's behalf.

Every customer runs on a different stack, so this role calls for real engineering depth, and you don't need a long AI resume to have it. We're looking for a strong developer who has recently put LLM-powered workflows into production. Plenty of people can prompt their way to a working prototype. We need someone who can own the code behind it, troubleshoot it inside an unfamiliar environment, and harden it so it holds up long after you've moved on to the next customer.

What You'll Do

Discovery and Scoping (with the AI Sales Lead)

  • Sit with customers' frontline staff to learn how the work actually gets done, capture the rules and exceptions that live in people's heads, and translate them into explicit logic
  • Build trust with the people whose work you're automating, and treat them as the experts on their process
  • Assess technical feasibility and identify which tasks are good candidates for an agent and where human review should stay in the loop
  • Translate customer needs into solution designs, effort estimates, and clear scope
  • Build proofs of concept and demos that show customers what an agent can do with their own workflows
  • Provide build and run cost estimates (model usage, infrastructure, maintenance) to support pricing
  • Join customer discovery calls to understand their workflows, systems, data, and pain points

Build and Deploy

  • Design, build, and deploy AI agents and automations that handle multi-step workflows across customer operations
  • Build and configure integrations that link each customer's tools, such as CRMs, ERPs, accounting platforms, email, messaging, and document storage, using APIs where they exist and browser automation where they don't
  • Write production-quality Python for integrations, data transformation, and agent tooling
  • Use SQL to validate agent outputs, reconcile records across systems, and measure accuracy
  • Build error handling, retries, idempotency, logging, alerting, and graceful fallbacks into everything you ship
  • Create testing and evaluation processes for each agent: test sets, regression checks, and accuracy tracking before go-live and after every change
  • Architect deployments so each customer's data, credentials, and permissions stay fully isolated

Handoff and Support

  • Hand off live agents to Operations Managers with runbooks, monitoring dashboards, review queues, and clear escalation paths
  • Train Operations Managers to supervise agent output, spot problems early, and handle routine exceptions without engineering help
  • Serve as the technical escalation point when an agent fails or a customer's systems change
  • Use what you learn from each deployment to build reusable components, templates, and deployment patterns that make the next customer faster to deliver
  • Measure and report impact for each customer against a baseline: hours saved, turnaround time, error rates, and cost per run

First-Year Mission

Your first year is measured by the operating results customers see, not by how many agents you deliver.

  • Establish a baseline for every customer workflow you take on: hours spent, turnaround time, error rates, and cost
  • Deliver measurable, sustained improvements against those baselines for customers across multiple industries
  • Shorten the time from signed agreement to measurable customer results
  • Hand off agents that Operations Managers run day to day with minimal engineering involvement
  • Earn renewals and expansions because the results hold up over time

Requirements

  • 3+ years of professional software engineering, solutions engineering, or automation engineering experience
  • Proof of recent production LLM workflows: something you built with Claude, OpenAI, or a similar platform that real users rely on
  • Strong Python: you structure, test, and debug your code, and you understand what AI-generated code is doing before you ship it
  • Strong SQL: joins, CTEs, window functions, and tracking down data quality problems
  • Browser automation experience with Playwright or a similar tool, for systems with limited or no APIs
  • Solid experience with REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth, pagination, and rate limits across a wide range of third-party platforms
  • A track record of troubleshooting production failures: reading logs and stack traces, isolating root causes, and fixing them permanently
  • Comfort with Bash and the command line for deployment, scheduling, and debugging
  • Git and version control as a standard part of how you work
  • Workflow discovery skills: you can interview the people who do the work, uncover the steps and exceptions they don't think to mention, and turn tacit knowledge into explicit rules
  • Operator empathy: you build trust with frontline staff, treat them as the experts on their work, and explain technical tradeoffs in plain language
  • Comfort in customer-facing settings: you can run a technical conversation with a customer and push back on scope when needed
  • Strong documentation habits, since the people running your agents day to day won't be engineers

jobs.excerpt: Terms of Reference (ToR): Rapid Assessment of the Context of and Opportunities for Refugees and Displaced Youth in Ghana.
jobs.companyName: World University Service of Canada (WUSC - EUMC)
jobs.description:
Terms of Reference (ToR): Rapid Assessment of the Context of and Opportunities for Refugees and Displaced Youth in Ghana.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Interested applicants are encouraged to submit their applications early.

1. Background

Ghana hosts refugees and asylum seekers from neighboring countries, including Côte d’Ivoire, Togo and Burkina Faso. In recent years, insecurity in the Sahel region, alongside climate-related pressures and intercommunal tensions, has contributed to increased displacement and cross-border movements, particularly affecting northern Ghana.

Within these populations, young people aged 18–35 face a range of barriers to education, skills development, employment and economic participation. These may include disrupted educational pathways, limited access to vocational training, difficulties accessing formal employment, documentation requirements, financial constraints and social exclusion. Young women and youth with disabilities may experience additional barriers. These barriers may be compounded by intersecting factors such as age, gender, disability, displacement status, socioeconomic circumstances and geographic location. Gender norms, unpaid care responsibilities, safety concerns and limited accessibility may further constrain participation in education and economic opportunities. However, the circumstances of displaced youth vary considerably depending on their legal status, location, socioeconomic conditions and access to institutional support. Opportunities for inclusion are also influenced by government policies, the capacities and incentives of relevant institutions, local labour-market conditions, and the availability of education and employment services.

The Mastercard Foundation, through its partnership with WUSC under the DREEM project, seeks to strengthen opportunities for refugees and displaced youth (RDPs) to access education, develop relevant skills and participate meaningfully in economic life.

A rapid contextual assessment is therefore proposed to consolidate existing evidence, examine the institutional and structural factors shaping RDP inclusion in Ghana, and identify practical opportunities for future programming, partnerships and policy engagement.

2. Purpose of the Assessment

The assessment aims to generate practical, context-specific evidence on the barriers and opportunities affecting the inclusion of refugees and displaced youth in education, skills development, employment and broader economic participation in Ghana.

It will examine the policy, institutional, socioeconomic and political economy factors shaping these opportunities, including the roles and incentives of relevant government institutions, education and training providers, private-sector actors, development partners and refugee-led organizations. The assessment will apply an intersectional lens to understand how barriers and opportunities differ among displaced youth, particularly young women, youth with disabilities and those experiencing multiple forms of exclusion.

The assessment will inform the Mastercard Foundation's and DREEM's understanding of the Ghanaian context and help identify feasible areas for programmatic support, institutional partnerships and policy engagement.

jobs.excerpt: Who You AreSwoogo is actively seeking a strategic, commercially minded, and accomplished Director, Enterprise Customer Success to set the vision for, build, and lead our Enterprise Customer Success organization.
jobs.description:
Who You Are

Swoogo is actively seeking a strategic, commercially minded, and accomplished Director, Enterprise Customer Success to set the vision for, build, and lead our Enterprise Customer Success organization. You will define how Swoogo creates, measures, and communicates value for its largest and most complex customers, and build a team of consultative, outcome-driven advisors who make Swoogo indispensable to their event and marketing strategies.

In this role, you will lead the Enterprise Customer Success Managers who support our largest customers, and you will be accountable for retention and influencing growth outcomes of the Enterprise portfolio. You will influence the evolution of the team making sure the team is optimally structured to drive outcomes for the customer and Swoogo, what our value framework and customer lifecycle look like, how we engage customer executives, and how we turn customer insight into product and company decisions. You will align with the VP, Customer Success, the VP of Accounts, and the Chief Customer Officer on commercial strategy, and be the senior voice of the Enterprise customer inside Swoogo. We are looking for a leader with a record of scaling teams that prove the business value of their customers' programs, commercial judgement, deep technical credibility, proven track record of leveraging AI to drive efficiencies, in depth knowledge of CSM workflows that enable you to effectively leverage AI so the team can focus on high impact work.

What You’ll Do

The ideal candidate for the Director, Enterprise Customer Success position is a strategic, collaborative leader who thrives within a demanding work environment and is energized by building teams and systems. They demonstrate executive presence, sound judgment, and a commitment to surpassing expectations, and they are skilled at influencing across the organization and with customer executives. Depending on customer requirements, the Director, Enterprise Customer Success may be needed to provide after-hours or weekend coverage for critical customer situations.

Every day will look a little different, but in general, you will do things like:

  • Set the strategy. Define the vision, strategy, and annual plan for Enterprise Customer Success in partnership with the VP, Customer Success, focused on value realization, customer experience, retention, and growth.
  • Define the value framework. Establish how Swoogo identifies customer value drivers, sets measurable outcomes, and demonstrates event ROI, such as registration conversion, attendee experience, pipeline influenced, and time and cost saved, and make that framework the standard across success plans, business reviews, and renewals.
  • Build a consultative, outcome-centric culture. Set the standard for discovery, account profiling, stakeholder mapping, objection handling, and executive storytelling, and create the enablement and coaching programs that make those habits the norm.
  • Own Enterprise retention. Be accountable for gross revenue retention for the Enterprise portfolio, and set the renewal strategy for complex, high-value accounts, including multi-year agreements and procurement engagement, in partnership with Account Management, who is responsible for the commercial negotiation.
  • Build a high performing enterprise CSM team. Hire, develop, and hold accountable the Enterprise Customer Success team, and build a strong bench through succession planning and career development.
  • Align on commercial strategy. Partner with the VP, Customer Success, the VP of Accounts, the Chief Customer Officer, and Sales leadership on renewal and expansion strategy, pricing and packaging input, key account plans, and support for strategic new-business opportunities.
  • Lead executive escalations. Serve as the senior escalation point for strategic customer issues, drive coordinated resolution across Support, Product, and Services, and lead root-cause analysis to prevent recurrence.
  • Run the operating cadence. Establish the health scoring, KPIs, and Executive Business Reviews for the Enterprise team, forecast renewals and risk, and report results and insights to executive leadership.
  • Be the voice of the customer. Bring structured customer insight into roadmap decisions with Product leadership, champion early adoption of new platform capabilities, and support customer advisory efforts.
  • Lead the technology and partner strategy. Position Swoogo within the customer's event and marketing technology stack, work with Services and technology and integration partners on complex implementations and expansion projects, and guide how the team uses AI to improve customer outcomes and team productivity.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives. Drive programs such as risk mitigation, renewal transformation, and adoption, working with Revenue Operations, Finance, and Enablement as needed, and own Customer Success operations and tooling across AI tools, Gainsight, Salesforce, and JIRA.
  • Plan and invest. Work with the VP, Customer Success on budget, headcount planning, and organizational design, and contribute to company-level planning and priorities.
  • Represent Swoogo. Engage with customers, partners, and industry events to share best practices and champion a culture of customer-centricity and a "deliver plus one" mindset.

What You’ve Done Before

  • 5 - 7 years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, Sales, Event Technology, Technology Consulting, or another customer-facing, revenue-carrying enterprise SaaS role, including 5+ years of people leadership with experience managing managers.
  • A proven record of improving gross and net revenue retention, expansion, and customer health across a portfolio of large, complex accounts.
  • Experience building a consultative, outcome-centric Customer Success organization, including value frameworks, playbooks, enablement, and coaching programs.
  • Proficiency with AI tools and an understanding of AI's impact on event and marketing teams.
  • A demonstrated ability to connect product capabilities to a customer's strategic goals and explain the value in plain, outcome-focused terms, and to teach others to do the same.
  • Strong commercial judgment, including experience with renewal strategy, complex negotiations, multi-year agreements, and procurement engagement, and with building expansion pipeline in partnership with Account Management.
  • Experience building and scaling Customer Success teams, including segmentation, coverage models, capacity planning, and operating cadences, and a clear view of how to scale engagement while still retaining and growing revenue.
  • Experience developing strategy and turning it into initiatives with clear owners, metrics, and results.
  • A background in event technology, marketing technology, or an adjacent software category serving marketers.
  • Expertise with Martech and enterprise systems, particularly integrations with Salesforce, Marketo, HubSpot, and Eloqua, and the IT systems that support end-to-end business processes across the customer's value chain.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate, present, and influence effectively at all levels of an organization, including executive and C-level stakeholders, with strong executive presence and storytelling.
  • A track record of collaborating cross-functionally with Sales, Product, Engineering, Services, Support, and Revenue Operations.
  • Sharp analytical judgment and operational excellence in forecasting, planning, and turning customer data into action.
  • Comfort making decisions in ambiguous or changing situations and leading through escalations with urgency, calm, and sound judgment.

It’d be Great if You’ve Done This

  • Experience supporting APAC customers with an understanding of GDPR and regional business nuances.
  • Experience with budget ownership, headcount planning, and organizational design for a Customer Success team.
  • Experience establishing an executive sponsor program or customer advisory board.
  • Experience engaging with technology partners and system integrators.
  • Familiarity with CRM tools (e.g., Gainsight, Salesforce) and event technology platforms.
  • Previous experience with Swoogo or similar event management tools.

Benefits, & How We Work

Learn moreabout Swoogo, how we work, and ourPerks & Benefits.

Swoogo is committed to providing a work environment free from discrimination, sexual harassment, and all forms of abusive conduct. We do not tolerate harassment or discrimination of any kind—whether committed by managers, peers, clients, or vendors. We strictly comply with all applicable employment laws, including Title VII of the Civil Rights Act, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), and the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA).

jobs.excerpt: Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits.
jobs.description:
Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits.

More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan. Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings.

We’re a high-growth fintech company changing the retirement industry. We are backed by a number of investors. This includes funding from Marshall Wace and Baillie Gifford, as well as top investors such as BlackRock, TPG (The Rise Fund), SoftBank, Glynn Capital, NewView Capital, USVP, Wing, Uncork, and more.

About the role

As the Manager, Customer Retention, you lead Human Interest's Retention team with the primary goal of proactively intervening with at-risk customers to drive positive retention outcomes. You own the team's performance and are responsible for ensuring members focus on the right accounts using the right approach. Collaborating closely with the Sr. Director, Customer Retention, who defines the overarching strategy, you turn strategic direction into everyday operational execution for the team. While you will directly lead high-stakes and sensitive save opportunities, your core responsibility is empowering and maximizing the overall effectiveness of your team.

About the team

The Retention team is a team in motion! The team is currently undergoing an exciting evolution, shifting from traditional reactive save efforts toward predictive outreach and proactive relationship management.

Joining now presents a unique opportunity: as we deliberately scale our structure and refine our metrics,
you will have a direct hand in shaping the function's playbook. If you thrive in an environment where your
customer insights can directly influence operational strategy, this is the ideal role for you.

What you get to do every day

  • Oversee team operations including full-cycle hiring, and onboarding. As well as, developing management playbooks, training materials, and talk tracks.
  • Own the team's performance against retention targets. Report results and forecasts to
    Leadership each month. Govern the use of concessions. Review and approve concessions
    within your delegated approval authority, escalate requests above it, and manage the team's
    overall use of concessions. Report results and forecasts to the Sr. Director, Customer Retention
    each month and contribute to monthly business reviews.
  • Run the daily operation of the retention case queue. This includes assigning new cases so
    workload is balanced and matched to experience, monitoring caseloads, and enforcing the
    team's rules of engagement on case ownership, same-day outreach, outreach cadence,
    documentation, and resolution coding so that reporting on saves and losses is accurate.
  • Act as Retention's primary partner to the leaders of Relationship Management, Customer
    Success Operations, Product, Sales and Onboarding, and Finance. Run the feedback loops that
    route churn root causes to the teams that own the improvements. Bring recurring patterns
    and their financial impact to the Sr. Director, Customer Retention for escalation.
  • Validating monthly commission calculations and submitting payouts on schedule. Contribute
    to the design of future incentive plans
  • Identify segments of retention volume that can be handled through automation or AI-assisted
    outreach, run pilots, and scale what works, while keeping people responsible for customer-facing judgment and pricing decisions. Make sure capacity freed by automation is actually spent on
    outreach to at-risk accounts.
  • As necessary, be personally involved in relationship-sensitive retention conversations, and use
    them to demonstrate the standards expected from the team.
  • Oversee team operations including full-cycle hiring, and onboarding. As well as, developing management playbooks, training materials, and talk tracks.
  • Other duties as assigned.

What you bring to the role

  • 6+ years of experience in customer retention, customer success, account management, or
    client-facing sales within financial services, fintech, or B2B SaaS.
  • 2+ years of experience directly managing a team.
    contributors, preferably a team paid partly on commission or measured against revenue targets.
  • A track record of improving retention or save outcomes at the team level, and the ability to
    explain specifically what you changed to get there.
  • Working knowledge of 401(k), 403(b), or other qualified plan administration, deep enough
    to coach reps through various retention scenarios and customer conversations.
  • Experience coaching negotiation and objection handling, including through structured
    review of recorded calls.
  • Comfort working with data. You can build and read Salesforce reports and dashboards,
    work in a BI tool such as Tableau, interpret trends and generate insights. .
  • Sound commercial judgment about concessions, including experience managing approvals
    within defined limits.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence peers and senior leaders in other functions who do not report
    to you.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including presenting results and recommendations
    to senior leadership.

Nice to have

  • Experience at a 401(k) recordkeeper, retirement plan provider, payroll company, or HR technology company serving small and mid-sized businesses.
  • QKA, QPA, RPF, or a similar retirement plan designation, or a commitment to earning one
    within 18 months in the role.
  • Experience managing a fully remote team.
  • Experience working with financial advisors and third-party administrators.
  • Bachelor's degree.

Why you will love working at Human Interest

Human Interest is tackling one of our country's biggest challenges - closing the retirement gap. You'll be instrumental in architecting and scaling solutions that bring financial security to employees at small and medium-sized businesses nationwide. We’ve made significant progress, but there is still growth ahead, offering you a unique opportunity to solve complex problems, drive innovation, and advance your career alongside a dedicated, mission-driven team. We value hard work and recognize that our team's contributions are key to our continued success.

Join Human Interest and make a lasting impact by shaping the future of retirement.

Our operating principles define how we work together as a team. They reflect Human Interest’s unique view on what’s important and what’s right. Documenting this core aspect of our culture helps employees make good decisions on their own. It also helps candidates considering career opportunities critically evaluate whether they will thrive at Human Interest.

The opportunity

Sensibly Sprouted is hiring a Registered Dietitian Manager with prior experience managing direct reports to independently lead a Dietetics team providing outpatient Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT). This established management role calls for someone ready to make sound hiring, performance, staffing, operational, and financial decisions and take responsibility for the team’s results.

Internally, this position is called Lead. You’ll lead interviewing and hiring as you build your team, coach and develop the dietitians you manage, and oversee the team as a business unit. Your primary responsibility is team leadership, with no fixed patient caseload. You may provide patient care as needed to support team capacity or coverage, subject to applicable licensure.

  • Lead interviewing, hiring, and onboarding as you build your team.
  • Coach and develop dietitians through regular one-on-ones, clear expectations, feedback, and performance management.
  • Own the team’s profit and loss (P&L), including revenue, expenses, and profitability, while managing retention and productive capacity. Use financial and performance data to guide decisions.
  • Manage staffing, workflows, and priorities while maintaining clinical, documentation, scheduling, and productivity standards.
  • Partner with Clinical Excellence on training needs, develop future leaders, and make decisions independently within your authority.

What you’ll bring

  • A Registered Dietitian (RD) or Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) credential.
  • Applicable state licensure, or eligibility to obtain required licensure.
  • Prior experience as a manager with direct reports, including hiring, coaching, staffing, and performance management.
  • Experience using operational and financial data to manage team capacity, revenue, expenses, and profitability.
  • Clear communication, sound judgment, dependable follow-through, and the ability to make decisions independently.
  • Authorization to work in the United States without employer sponsorship.

Your growth

Lead is an established management role with room to deepen your business judgment, strengthen team results, and develop future leaders. Managers who sustain strong business results, develop other leaders, and contribute beyond their own team may be considered for Senior Lead when an opportunity is available. Starting pay reflects directly transferable leadership and business capability; growth within the Lead salary range reflects sustained effectiveness in this role.

We are a team of registered dietitians providing personalized, evidence-based nutrition counseling and Medical Nutrition Therapy. Our care emphasizes ongoing patient relationships and practical changes that fit real life.

About Us

We are a stealth-stage fund and tech startup operating at the intersection of alternative markets and quantitative strategy. Backed by experienced operators and growing quickly, we are building the infrastructure to scale a high-performance, data-driven business.

We are a lean team with outsized ambition. Almost everything we do runs on software we built ourselves, and the pace of the business is now set by how good that software is.

The Role

You will own our internal platform. It is what our operations, finance and delivery teams work in every day: the systems that move money, track work, sync communications, and tell us what is actually happening in the business.

One person built most of it. You are taking it over, making it something the company can depend on rather than something one person holds in their head, and then extending it.

This is not a product engineering job with a designer, a product manager and a groomed backlog. You will sit with the people doing the work, find the thing costing them the most hours, and go fix it. Judgment about what to build matters more here than depth in any particular stack.

What You'll Do

Take over what exists. Learn the running systems, document them properly, and get them to a state where they are not dependent on any single person, including you.

Give the business its numbers. Several of the things leadership most needs to see are not currently visible anywhere. You will build the data capture and reporting that changes that, starting from agreed definitions rather than a blank dashboard.

Turn spreadsheets into systems. A lot of important work still lives in shared sheets with no state, no ownership and no history. You will move it into the platform, one workflow at a time.

Find the constraint and remove it. There is far more to build than one person can build. The job is choosing correctly, repeatedly, and being able to explain the choice.

Be the person who says where things stand. Short weekly written updates, honest dates, early warnings when something is going to slip. Leadership should never have to ask.

Work directly with the founder. No layers.

Requirements

  • You have been the engineer an operations team depended on. Ideally you were early at a startup and built the internal systems the company ran on.

The AIR Opportunity Fund is seeking a Senior Program Officer to support and advance the Fund’s grantmaking, research, and partnership activities focused on expanding opportunity and improving outcomes for communities across the United States. The selected candidate will work remotely but must be based in or near one of the Fund's priority regions: the Midwest (Chicago or Cleveland preferred), the greater Washington, DC, area, or the Delta Region (Arkansas, Alabama, or Mississippi preferred).   • Experience managing or supporting grant portfolios, philanthropic initiatives, research projects, or community-based programs.

  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build productive relationships across a variety of stakeholders.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Flosum is a bootstrapped, profitable B2B SaaS company building the leading Salesforce-native DevSecOps, Data Protection, and Security platform. Our solutions are trusted by Fortune 500 enterprises in the most heavily regulated industries on the planet — financial services, healthcare, government, and insurance.

We’re not a startup burning cash and chasing vanity metrics. We’re a proven, scaling business that reached profitability on our own terms. As a Salesforce Summit Partner and Innovation Award winner, we’ve earned our seat at the table alongside the biggest names in enterprise software.

Built 100% on the Salesforce platform. Serving enterprises that demand zero compromise on security, compliance, and reliability.

Why This Role Exists

We are entering an aggressive growth phase — expanding our product surface, deepening our platform capabilities, and accelerating our delivery velocity. We need senior-caliber Node.js developers who can own significant parts of our architecture and ship production code that enterprise customers depend on daily.

This is not a staff augmentation seat. You will work directly with engineering leadership, product managers, and the CEO. Your decisions will have real consequences, your opinions will be heard, and your craftsmanship will be visible to the customers who rely on our platform.

What You’ll Build

  • High-performance backend services and APIs powering enterprise-grade SaaS applications
  • Scalable, secure Node.js micro services and integrations within the Salesforce ecosystem
  • Modern front-end experiences using Vue.js and TypeScript that serve demanding enterprise users
  • CI/CD pipeline tooling, automation frameworks, and developer productivity infrastructure
  • Real-time data processing and event-driven architectures handling sensitive enterprise data at scale

Requirements

Read this section carefully. We are specific about what we need because we are serious about who we hire.

Non-Negotiable Technical Requirements

  • 5+ years of professional Node.js development in production environments — not tutorials, not side projects, not bootcamp exercises. Real production systems serving real users at scale.
  • Expert-level understanding of asynchronous programming, event loops, streams, and the Node.js runtime. You should be able to explain backpressure, the differences between setImmediate and process.nextTick, and why unhandled promise rejections are dangerous — without Googling it.
  • Deep experience with TypeScript in production codebases. We write typed code, and we expect you to understand why.
  • Strong command of RESTful API design, authentication patterns (OAuth 2.0, JWT), and API security best practices for enterprise environments.
  • Proven experience with SQL and NoSQL databases, query optimization, data modeling, and understanding the performance implications of schema decisions at scale.
  • Proficiency with Git workflows, code review practices, automated testing (unit, integration, and end-to-end), and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Solid understanding of containerization (Docker), cloud services (AWS/GCP/Azure), and infrastructure-as-code principles.

Highly Preferred (These Will Set You Apart)

  • Salesforce development experience: Apex, Lightning Web Components (LWC), Visualforce, or Salesforce API integrations. If you know both Node.js and Salesforce, you are a rare and extremely valuable candidate to us.
  • Experience building or contributing to Salesforce ISV (AppExchange) products.
  • Vue.js front-end development experience, particularly with Vue 3 Composition API and state management.
  • Experience working in B2B SaaS companies serving enterprise customers with strict compliance requirements (SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR).
  • Familiarity with DevOps/DevSecOps toolchains and practices in the Salesforce ecosystem.

The Kind of Person We’re Looking For

Skills get you in the door. Mindset determines whether you thrive here:

Missionary, Not Mercenary

You care about what you’re building and why. You take ownership not because someone assigned it to you, but because that’s who you are. When something is broken at 2 AM, you don’t check whether it’s “your responsibility” — you fix it.

Builder, Not a Bystander

You don’t wait for perfect specifications. You dig in, ask hard questions, propose solutions, and ship. You would rather have a working prototype by Friday than a polished slide deck by next quarter.

Craftsperson Under Pressure

Enterprise customers depend on our uptime and data integrity. You write code that doesn’t just work — it survives. You understand that in regulated industries, your code is your reputation.

Direct Communicator

You say what you think, respectfully and clearly. If a technical decision is wrong, you speak up — regardless of who made it. We value candor over politeness-at-the-expense-of-quality.

This Is a Long-Term Commitment

Let us be direct: we are not looking for contractors who jump between projects every few months. We are building a world-class engineering team, and we invest heavily in the people who join us. In return, we expect commitment.

This role is designed as a long-term, full-time engagement. You will grow with us. You will own systems end-to-end. You will see the direct impact of your work in how Fortune 500 companies build, protect, and deploy on Salesforce.

If you’re looking for a short-term gig while you wait for something else, this isn’t the role. If you want to build something that matters and be part of a team that’s scaling from strong to dominant, keep reading.

Benefits

  • Direct collaboration with the founding team and engineering leadership — your voice will carry weight from day one
  • A profitable, stable company with aggressive growth plans — no funding anxiety, no runway clock

  • Meaningful technical challenges: security, compliance, scale, and reliability at the intersection of Node.js and Salesforce

  • Remote-first flexibility with a results-oriented work environment
