Make an Impact as a Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) AI Lead at Worldwide


Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how organizations operate, and effective governance is essential to ensuring that innovation happens responsibly. As the Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) AI Lead, you will play a central role in shaping how AI is governed across Worldwide Clinical Trials.


You will build and lead the Enterprise IT AI Governance framework, creating practical, risk-based processes for AI systems, AI-enabled technologies, and AI agents throughout their lifecycle. From initial use-case evaluation and approval through ongoing monitoring and retirement, you will help ensure AI is adopted securely, responsibly, and in alignment with regulatory, contractual, and business requirements.


This is a highly collaborative role where you will partner with business owners and experts across Information Security, Privacy, Legal, Quality, Enterprise Architecture, Data, Vendor Management, and Procurement. You will bring these perspectives together while maintaining clear accountability and enabling teams to pursue AI opportunities with appropriate controls and human oversight.


Where You'll Work


This is a remote role open to candidates based in the US. You will collaborate with global teams across multiple time zones.


What You'll Do


  • Build and maintain the Enterprise IT AI Governance framework, including the operating model, standards, procedures, decision rights, risk tiers, controls, and governance records.
  • Establish a company-wide intake, assessment, and approval process for AI use cases, AI-enabled vendor products, internally developed solutions, and AI agents.
  • Maintain a centralized inventory of AI systems and agents, capturing ownership, intended use, data sources, permissions, dependencies, risk classification, approval status, and lifecycle information.
  • Lead risk-based governance reviews in partnership with Information Security, Privacy, Legal, Quality, Enterprise Architecture, Data, Vendor Management, Procurement, and other subject-matter experts.
  • Define governance requirements for AI agents, including ownership, approved purpose, identity and access, human oversight, testing, monitoring, logging, change control, incident response, and secure retirement.
  • Coordinate reviews of cybersecurity, privacy, quality, third-party, and operational risks associated with AI, including sensitive data exposure, prompt injection, excessive agency, insecure integrations, identity misuse, unauthorized actions, and supply-chain dependencies.
  • Strengthen governance for clinical, GxP, and other regulated AI use cases by partnering with Quality and business owners on validation, human oversight, data integrity, change control, recordkeeping, and inspection readiness.
  • Monitor approved AI technologies for material changes, control exceptions, incidents, performance concerns, and emerging requirements, triggering reassessment and remediation when appropriate.
  • Deliver practical governance guidance, training, metrics, executive reporting, and audit-ready evidence while advising leadership on emerging AI risks, governance gaps, and investment needs.

What You'll Bring


  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Data Science, Risk Management, Business, Law, or a related field; an advanced degree is preferred.
  • 8+ years of progressive experience in governance, risk and compliance, technology risk, cybersecurity, privacy, data governance, audit, quality, or a related discipline, including 3+ years leading enterprise governance programs, cross-functional risk initiatives, or technology control frameworks.
  • Demonstrated experience developing policies, standards, risk assessments, control requirements, governance workflows, metrics, and executive reporting.
  • Working experience with AI governance, responsible AI, generative AI, machine learning, automation, AI-enabled vendor products, or AI agent governance is strongly preferred.

Responsibilities for this Position

General Dynamics Mission Systems has an immediate opening for a Mission Architect focused on embedded security, anti-tamper, operating system and hypervisor security, avionics, and tactical radios and networks. This role pairs deep technical mission architecture with business development responsibility: the successful candidate will serve as a principal technical authority who shapes government customer requirements, architects winning technical solutions, and leads capture of new government-funded R&D programs. This is an opportunity to grow a portfolio of defense cyber R&D and anti-tamper business by combining credible technical leadership with the relationship-building, capture, and proposal skills of a business development leader. General Dynamics Mission Systems employees work closely with esteemed customers to develop solutions that allow them to carry out high-stakes national security missions.

REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES AND TASKS

  • Directs business development activities for embedded security, OS/hypervisor security, and anti-tamper R&D offerings to government agencies and firms performing government business
  • Serves as principal technical architect and capture manager for assigned new-business opportunities, translating mission needs into research roadmaps, technical solutions, and win strategies
  • Maintains key business development and technical relationships with government program offices, research laboratories, defense industrial base primes, and subcontractor teams
  • Partners with account teams on fielded embedded security and anti-tamper programs to identify incremental sustainment and technology-refresh opportunities, while prioritizing new R&D program capture
  • Evaluates and manages new business opportunities, initiatives, partnerships, alliances, and joint ventures in secure computing, embedded OS, avionics, and tactical networking
  • Oversees market analysis, monitors competitive R&D activity, and identifies emerging mission gaps and new program starts across the embedded security and anti-tamper customer base
  • Defines vision, strategy, and tactics for assigned business development pursuits, including technology roadmaps spanning embedded security, secure processing, anti-tamper, and cyber resilience
  • Authors and directs proposal development for government R&D opportunities, drawing on direct technical expertise to strengthen technical volumes and win themes
  • Advises higher management on status and recommended action for existing and potential business development opportunities across the embedded security portfolio
  • Provides technical and business leadership in the planning, design, due diligence, and implementation of strategic objectives for the embedded security and tactical systems portfolio
  • Represents the company at technical conferences, industry days, and government technology demonstration events
  • Leads and mentors multidisciplinary engineering teams supporting technical capture and solution development
  • Develops and monitors profitability, productivity, and growth targets for the assigned technology and business area

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES

  • Demonstrates tremendous experience defining and executing successful strategies to grow government R&D business in embedded security, anti-tamper, or related technical domains
  • Able to articulate examples of having conceived, architected, and led novel technical research efforts through to funded programs and transitioned capabilities
  • Able to articulate examples of having identified, pursued, and won large capture efforts in areas related to GDMS business
  • Possesses broad market awareness, including government budgets, customer priorities, mission gaps, and market dynamics across embedded security and anti-tamper
  • Credible as a technical authority among engineering peers, program customers, and executive leadership on operating systems / hypervisors, anti-tamper, and embedded security topics
  • Demonstrates tremendous interpersonal, communication, collaboration, and leadership skills; thrives in a highly interactive team environment spanning technical, program, and business development functions
  • Recognized ability to build relationships with senior-level customers and internal counterparts
  • May require an understanding of international business and export processes
  • Works well under pressure with the ability to simultaneously deliver on multiple tasks and priorities
  • Top level of management below the Executive Team, usually reporting to a Vice President; directs the activities of a functional area, business area, or major program through lower management levels
  • Participates with other senior managers to establish strategic plans and objectives; expected to make final decisions in conjunction with the Executive Team on business, operational, or programmatic matters
  • Works on complex technical and business issues where analysis requires in-depth knowledge of the company and of embedded security domain
  • Regularly interacts with executives and/or major customers, conducting business and technical briefings for senior and top management and external representatives
  • Interactions frequently involve negotiating with customers, partners, or management, and influencing senior-level leaders regarding matters of significance to the organization
  • Performance metrics visible at the GDMS, business, or functional level; erroneous decisions will have a serious impact on the overall success of functional, division, or company operations
  • Has overall control of planning, staffing, budgeting, and managing expense priorities; responsible for managing people, including performance evaluations, pay increase recommendations, and hire/fire decisions

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent is required plus a minimum of 10 years of demonstrated experience generating and capturing government-funded research and development business; or Master's degree plus a minimum of 8 years of demonstrated experience.
  • Minimum of 10 years of experience authoring and leading proposal captures for government-funded research and development programs, with demonstrated success winning funded awards
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience serving as a principal investigator or technical authority on funded government research efforts
  • Experience leading or directly contributing to multiple concurrent government research programs
  • Direct, hands-on research and engineering experience — not solely oversight or program management — in at least two of the following mission areas: operating system or hypervisor security; embedded or tactical computing platform security; avionics or other flight-safety-critical embedded systems; tactical radio and tactical network systems
  • Direct experience developing, integrating, or transitioning Anti-Tamper (AT) or cyber security technologies into customer systems, including familiarity with DoD Anti-Tamper policy and DoD Cyber Security / Zero Trust policy
  • Experience growing and leading a technical team supporting research capture and / or program delivery
  • Experience directing or technically evaluating subcontractor support on government research programs
  • Working knowledge of government contracting and acquisition practices

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct, hands-on research and engineering experience spanning all the mission areas above — operating system/hypervisor security, embedded/tactical platform security, avionics, and tactical radio/network systems — rather than a subset
  • Graduate degree with a completed thesis or other sustained research effort directly relevant to secure systems, distributed systems, or network security
  • A record of authored or co-authored technical publications or conference proceedings in relevant government or industry venues
  • Experience curating and presenting research at government-sponsored technology demonstration events (e.g., Service-sponsored conferences, rodeos, technology interchange meetings, or similar government/industry technical forums)
  • Experience growing an internal research organization from an individual-contributor effort into a multidisciplinary engineering team, including mentoring staff into senior or technical-lead roles
  • Experience serving as a technical interface across multiple simultaneous government customer contracts and organizations
  • Background spanning both classified defense program work and product-oriented R&D transition into fielded or commercial capabilities
  • Familiarity with GDMS Idaho Scientific's product portfolio, including Helios, Bedrock, and Keystone

Salary Note

This estimate represents the typical salary range for this position based on experience and other factors (geographic location, etc.). Actual pay may vary. This job posting will remain open until the position is filled.

jobs.description:
Not all heroes wear capes — but plenty of them use toilet paper

Want to challenge yourself at a purpose-led scale up AND make a difference in the world? Come join the revolootion!

Funny name, serious business

We make eco-friendly products and donate 50% of our profits to provide clean water and help build toilets for the billions of people who lack proper access. So far, we’ve contributed over $18 million AUD (roughly $12.5 million USD) to fund sanitation projects around the globe. Basically, we’re really good at doing good.

With hubs in Australia, the Philippines, China, the US, UK and Europe, our amazing team of 200+ work to make the biggest possible impact for people and the planet. Over the next couple of years, we’re hoping to increase our annual donation tenfold to get us closer to our dream of everyone in the world having access to clean water and sanitation services.

A bit about the role

This is a 6-month, fixed-term role supporting payroll for our Philippines hub. You’ll work closely with business leaders and our Payroll Lead to check PH payroll invoices, resolve any discrepancies, and collate everything into one clean file ready for review each pay cycle. It’s a finance-side role — think careful admin and attention to detail in Excel or Google Sheets, not managing a payroll system.

If you worked here this past month here are some things you might have been involved in

  • Checked payroll invoices for the PH hub with business leaders to confirm hours and amounts were accurate.
  • Collated the month’s invoices into a single file ready for the Payroll Lead’s review.
  • Chased up a business leader for a missing invoice ahead of the payroll deadline.
  • Updated the PH payroll tracker to reflect the latest pay cycle.

Let’s talk about you

You’ve got payroll in your bones (at least 5 years of it)

You’ve spent 5+ years in payroll, ideally on the finance side rather than the HR side, and you know your way around invoices, pay cycles and the occasional discrepancy that needs chasing down.

Excel (or Sheets) is basically your happy place

You don’t need to have used a fancy payroll system before — what you do need is to be genuinely comfortable building and maintaining accurate files in Excel or Google Sheets, because that’s how this role runs.

You’re organised, detail-obsessed and easy to work with

You like things tidy, you catch the small errors before they become big ones, and you’re comfortable chasing business leaders for the odd missing invoice without losing your cool.

You give a crap

Do you want your work to make the world a better place? Do you want to work with other people who feel the same way? What a coincidence — us too!

Why should you work with us?

First off,as a certified B Corp™, we work to make a difference every day while maintaining the highest standards of social and environmental impact. With our most recent score of 125.5 we’re in very good company with other exceptional B Corps around the world.

We also believe that helping to make the world a better place should be rewarded accordingly – that’s why we offer competitive, market informed salaries, meaningful support towards healthcare for our team around the world,generous paid leave, tailored learning and development opportunities, and free toilet paper (yes, you read that right).

Our engagement surveys (thanks Culture Amp!) tell us that our team is really proud (95%) to work for Who Gives A Crap and, well, we couldn’t be more proud of that.

Have you made it this far?

If you’re still reading, we think there’s a strong chance you might be our kind of person. Here’s the thing, though — research suggests that 60% of women and underrepresented folks might have already talked themselves out of applying. Even if you don’t check every box above, we want to encourage you to introduce yourself. We believe a diversity of perspectives and experiences makes a team stronger — and the stronger our team, the closer we are to delivering toilets and clean water for all.

jobs.excerpt: About the jobThe SOC Analyst is responsible for the continuous monitoring, triage, and investigation of security events across the organization's environment, as part of a global follow-the-sun Security Operations Center.
jobs.description:
About the job

The SOC Analyst is responsible for the continuous monitoring, triage, and investigation of security events across the organization's environment, as part of a global follow-the-sun Security Operations Center. This position reports to the SOC Lead. The role goes beyond acknowledging alerts: the focus is on understanding what each alert means, investigating suspicious activity end to end, responding to real threats, and handing over cleanly between regions so that nothing is lost across shifts. The ideal candidate has solid SOC experience, a strong investigative mindset, and thrives in a fast-paced, fully remote setting where accuracy, discipline, and security are essential. Hands-on engineering experience with core security platforms is a big plus.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor, triage, and analyze security alerts and events from the organization's security stack, including SIEM, Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), Security Service Edge (SSE), and Web Application Firewall (WAF) platforms.

  • Investigate security incidents end to end, from initial triage through analysis, containment, eradication, and post-incident documentation, coordinating with relevant teams throughout.

  • Determine the scope, severity, and impact of security events, separating true positives from false positives and escalating confirmed incidents according to defined procedures.

  • Execute response actions within the security platforms, such as isolating endpoints, blocking indicators, disabling compromised accounts, and enforcing access restrictions.

  • Ensure structured, high-quality shift handovers across regions in the follow-the-sun model, so that open investigations, ongoing incidents, and pending actions continue seamlessly around the clock.

  • Proactively threat hunt across endpoint, network, and log data to uncover suspicious activity that existing detections may have missed, mapping findings to frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK.

  • Provide feedback on detection quality and contribute to the tuning of SIEM correlation rules, EDR custom detections, and WAF rules to reduce noise and improve coverage.

  • Enrich investigations with threat intelligence, including indicators of compromise, attacker techniques, and emerging campaigns relevant to the organization.

  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, standard operating procedures, and incident response playbooks.

  • Collaborate with IT, infrastructure, application, and security engineering teams to resolve incidents and support day-to-day operations.

  • Support vulnerability management and drive continuous improvement of the organization's overall security posture.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

  • At least 3 years of hands-on experience as a SOC Analyst, triaging alerts and investigating security incidents in a production environment.

  • Solid working knowledge of core security technologies such as EDR, SSE, SIEM, and WAF, and of how to use them to investigate and respond to threats.

  • Hands-on experience implementing, configuring, and tuning these platforms, or writing and tuning detection content, is a big plus.

  • Experience with incident response and threat hunting, ideally with familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

  • Excellent understanding of network security, endpoint security, cloud security, and Zero Trust principles.

  • Relevant certifications such as Security+, CySA+, GCIA, GCIH, BTL1, or vendor-specific credentials are a plus.

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills with a high attention to detail.

  • Ability to handle sensitive information responsibly and securely.

  • Good written and verbal communication skills in English, and the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams and across time zones.

About You

You are a hands-on security analyst who wants to understand what is really happening behind an alert, rather than only closing tickets. You dig into the data, follow the evidence, and know when and how to escalate. If you have also stood up or tuned the tools you work with, or written your own detections, even better. You are structured, reliable, and comfortable working independently in a remote, follow-the-sun team, and you take pride in leaving a clear handover for the next shift. You are curious about new threats and technologies, and you enjoy working closely with both technical teams and end users to raise the security bar across the environment.

jobs.description:
We are looking for a Senior DevOps Engineer to join the MOSK (Mirantis OpenStack for Kubernetes) product team, working at the intersection of OpenStack, Kubernetes, and product engineering. In this role, you will help design, validate, and evolve a cloud-native OpenStack platform that enables customers to build and operate enterprise-grade private clouds at scale.

As a senior engineer, you will act as a technical authority on OpenStack and MOSK behavior, contribute to architectural decisions, support complex customer scenarios, and help ensure stable, high-quality product releases.

Key Responsibilities

Feature Design & Development

  • Contribute to Product Roadmap: Actively influence the MOSK roadmap and backlog by providing technical input on feature feasibility, architectural scalability, and long-term maintainability. Evaluate incoming customer requests for specific features by analyzing upstream OpenStack code, specifications, blueprints, and community documentation to assess feature maturity, stability, limitations, and operational caveats.
  • Lifecycle Management Engineering: Design, implement, and document lifecycle management for OpenStack on Kubernetes — a core MOSK capability — with emphasis on non-disruptive upgrades, patching, scaling, rollback strategies, and feature compatibility across upgrades.
  • Feature Validation & Integration: Drive validation of enabled features by defining test scenarios, validating upstream code behavior in simulated or production-like deployments, and then integrating feature support into MOSK’s lifecycle management.
  • Technical Design Reviews: Review and refine product designs, APIs, and implementations to ensure robustness, security, and a high-quality developer experience.
  • Engineering Leadership: Lead design discussions, planning sessions, and retrospectives; help the team to uphold high standards for software quality, architectural rigor, and operational readiness.

Product Engineering & Automation

  • Frameworks & Tooling Development: Design, implement, and maintain core frameworks, libraries, and internal tools that underpin MOSK development, testing, and lifecycle operations.
  • Advanced Automation: Build and evolve automation for deploying and managing complex OpenStack-on-Kubernetes environments used in development, testing, and validation.
  • CI/CD Architecture: Design, build, and maintain CI/CD pipelines and integrations with external systems to streamline build, test, validation, upgrade, and release workflows.

Operational Reliability

  • Tier-3 Escalation Support: Debug and resolve complex issues in customer production environments involving Kubernetes, OpenStack, networking, storage, and distributed systems.
  • Upstream Troubleshooting & Contributions: Investigate issues in OpenStack services, analyze root causes at the code level, and propose or contribute minor fixes upstream to improve product stability and supportability.
  • Performance & Scalability Analysis: Identify and analyze performance bottlenecks across hardware and software layers; provide fixes, optimizations, and tuning recommendations.
  • Operational Readiness: Manage and improve development, staging, and validation environments that closely mirror customer deployments to ensure release stability.
  • Product Knowledge Authority: Act as an authoritative technical source for MOSK and OpenStack behavior, providing accurate, engineering-level input to documentation, field, and enablement teams to ensure correctness and consistency of product documentation and guidance. Participate in technical reviews, demos, and knowledge-sharing sessions to support engineering and other customer-facing teams.

Experience & Education

  • At least 5 years of practical administration experience in Linux (CentOS, Ubuntu, RHEL) as a server platform.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.
  • Experience in software development, Systems Administration, or SRE role.

Technical Skills

  • Operating Systems: Deep understanding of the OS, ability to debug and tune underperforming systems, and troubleshoot software and hardware issues.
  • Networking: Strong knowledge of networking technologies, including protocols, firewalls, and VPNs. Experience with managing and configuring networking equipment.
  • Automation Tools: Practical experience with SaltStack, Puppet, Ansible, or Chef for medium and large environments.
  • Infrastructure as Code: Practical experience with Terraform.
  • Containerization: Be an expert in Docker and Kubernetes in production environments. Thorough understanding and practical experience with Kubernetes operators and Helm.
  • CI/CD: Strong experience with Jenkins and building dependable build/release pipelines.
  • Familiarity with code-review systems
  • Cloud Platforms: Understanding of principles of working in cloud environments such as OpenStack, AWS, GCP, or Azure.
  • Scripting & Programming: Strong scripting skills in Bash, Groovy, and Python (at least one is required). Mid-level experience with Go or C is valuable.

Preferred Qualifications (Will be a plus)

  • Deep understanding of OpenStack architecture and experience with running it in production.
  • Knowledge and experience with SDN (Software Defined Networking) solutions - Open Virtual Network, Open vSwitch.
  • Experience in managing and using Open Search, Grafana, and Prometheus stacks.
  • Contribution to open-source projects.

Soft Skills

  • English language proficiency at least at an intermediate level (spoken and written).
  • Good customer-facing communication skills and a sense of diplomacy.
  • Ability to work with geographically distributed international teams in a dynamic environment.
  • Analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.

What does Mirantis offer you?

  • Work in a global, collaborative, remote-first culture that rewards initiative and execution.

  • Play a pivotal role in shaping the next era of cloud and AI modernisation.

  • Manage high-impact enterprise accounts with immediate opportunity for growth.

  • Work with exceptionally passionate, talented and engaging colleagues, helping Fortune 500 and Global 2000 customers implement next-generation cloud technologies.

  • Be a part of cutting-edge, open-source innovation.

  • Thrive in the high-energy environment of a young company where openness, collaboration, risk-taking, and continuous growth are valued.

  • Attend conferences and working groups.

  • Customized workstation (macOS, Windows).

  • Professional development and training.

  • Competitive compensation, performance incentives, and opportunities for advancement.

Mirantis is the Kubernetes-native AI infrastructure company, enabling organizations to build and operate scalable, secure, and sovereign infrastructure for modern AI, machine learning, and data-intensive applications. jobs.title: Procurement Finance & Data Associate
jobs.excerpt: What does the Company do? Fortune 1,000 companies spend billions with 1,000s of suppliers.
jobs.description:
What does the Company do?

Fortune 1,000 companies spend billions with 1,000s of suppliers. We represent these large companies and save them money by negotiating pricing with their suppliers. Teams at these large companies are focused on their large suppliers and typically don’t actively manage the mid/smaller suppliers as closely. We help solve this problem by negotiating directly with this subset of suppliers and deliver meaningful savings within just a few months. We work with our clients on a project basis and have executed more than 50,000 negotiations across 90+ countries.

We intentionally have a very limited online presence (including LinkedIn) – the best way to find out more is to have a chat. We are a fast-paced and entrepreneurial organization. We’ve been recognized for multiple years as one of Canada’s Fastest Growing Companies and a Great Place to Work.

What is the role?

Every savings number we bring to a client gets tested. Their procurement and finance teams will push on it, and it has to hold up. We need a finance professional who takes ownership of that: someone who checks the numbers and makes sure they’re accurate and defensible before they reach the client.

A lot of that checking is the same work every time, which makes it a great fit for automation. AI can now handle the data cleanup, classification and first-pass checks that used to eat up hours. We’re looking for someone with a solid finance background who enjoys building AI tools and always wants to find a faster, smarter way to do the work.

You’ll be part of the Procurement Excellence team, working with analysts and negotiators toward a shared savings target that everyone pitches in to hit. It’s an energetic group: people celebrate big wins and push hard to put more dollars on the board. If you like small, high-performing teams and making a real impact with Fortune 1000 clients, you’ll feel at home here.

Responsibilities

Savings validation

  • Review, validate and quantify the savings our team negotiates. The volume is high: you’ll review hundreds of unique outcomes in detail each year.
  • Build AI-assisted first-pass checks that flag anomalies, so your judgement goes where it matters most.
  • Work directly with vendors to resolve questions about their savings proposals.
  • Work directly with clients to make sure negotiated savings are understood and implemented correctly, and track implementation with dashboards.

Build: AI-enabled data workflows

  • Design, build and maintain AI-assisted workflows that ingest, cleanse, normalize and classify large client spend data sets (>1 million lines) from P2P and ERP systems (e.g., SAP, Ariba, Coupa).
  • Apply generative AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot) alongside Power Query, Power Automate and/or Python to automate supplier name normalization, spend categorization and data extraction from contracts, invoices and vendor proposals.
  • Build reusable templates, prompts and playbooks so that every new client engagement is faster than the last.
  • Spot repetitive manual work across the team and automate it.

Build: Power BI reporting layer

  • Own our Power BI reporting layer end to end – data models, Power Query transformations, DAX measures and dashboards.
  • Build client-facing dashboards that track spend in scope, negotiation progress and savings negotiated vs. validated vs. implemented.
  • Build internal dashboards that give the team real-time visibility into pipeline and progress against the team savings target.
  • Maintain data quality, refresh schedules and governance so the numbers are always trusted.

What we’re looking for

  • Minimum 8 years of experience structuring and analyzing large data sets using Excel (PivotTables, lookups, etc.), and very large data sets using Power BI, including hands-on data modeling, Power Query and DAX
  • Demonstrated experience building with AI – you have used generative AI tools to automate a data or analytical workflow, and can show us what you built
  • Working knowledge of at least one of SQL, Python or Power Automate (or a similar low-code tool), and the drive to keep learning new tools fast
  • Minimum 5 years of experience working in a client service setting (e.g., consulting, financial services)
  • Minimum 3 years of experience working closely with the Procurement function (e.g., savings validation, spend data analysis)
  • A builder mindset – when you see a repetitive task, your first question is “how do I make sure nobody does this manually again?”
  • Sound judgement with AI – you know when to trust an output, when to verify it, and how to protect confidential client data
  • You must be driven and gritty – our pace of work can be very intense at times!
  • You must be able to operate independently with limited oversight
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including turning data into a clear story for senior stakeholders

Nice to have

  • Microsoft PL-300 (Power BI Data Analyst) certification, or experience with Microsoft Fabric / Azure
  • Experience building AI agents or multi-step automations
  • Exposure to spend analytics or spend cube tools

Perks

  • Fully remote work – work from anywhere as long as you are available 9–5 ET - we do prioritize the Greater Toronto Area
  • Charitable donations – we donate a portion of the savings generated to a charity ($40K+ and counting)
  • Matching program for retirement savings accounts
  • Excellent benefits package
  • Training stipend

Given our growth, we’re looking to expand our team today. If the above sounds interesting, we’d love to have a chat!

This posting is for an existing vacancy. We do not use artificial intelligence to screen, assess or select applicants.

jobs.title: Operations Associate (Hiring or Client Delivery)
jobs.excerpt: Grow our AI image service. Before you apply, spend ten minutes on our website and LinkedIn.
jobs.description:
Grow our AI image service.

Before you apply, spend ten minutes on our website and LinkedIn. In your Loom we will ask what we do, where you found out about us, and why you want to work at Drop Zero Digital. Answers that could be about any company will not pass.

The role

We are Drop Zero Digital, a lifecycle marketing agency. We are hiring one person who is good at deciding. Our AI image service is our fastest-growing service, and whichever area you own, you will be helping it grow.

You will own one named area. Which one is decided during the trial rather than now, based on what you turn out to be strong at. It will be one of these two:

  1. The hiring machine. How we find, screen and hire people. Running the funnel end to end, sourcing, chasing, scheduling, keeping our tracker honest, and telling us when the process itself is broken.
  2. Client delivery operations. How work gets planned, briefed, chased and shipped for our clients. Holding timelines, briefing the team properly, and making sure nothing quietly stalls.

Both are the same job underneath: you notice what has slipped, you decide what to do, and you close it without being asked.

This is not an assistant job and it is not a coordinator job. You will make real calls every day, and you will be judged on the quality of those calls rather than on how much you got through.

We are building a team of people who decide well without being managed. If you want to be told what to do each morning, this job is not for you.

What we are looking for

  1. You make decisions and you own them, including the ones that go wrong.
  2. You can tell which calls are yours and which are not, and you get that split right in both directions.
  3. You take feedback as information and change, without folding on something you have good reason to believe.
  4. You get better fast. We would rather have someone at seventy percent climbing than someone flat at eighty five.
  5. You spot when something is failing and say so, including when it is our process and not your work.
  6. You write clearly and honestly, especially about problems.

On experience

We do not ask for a number of years. We check your work history against what you tell us, and a false answer ends the application.

Whatever employment you do list, we verify: employer, dates, title and paid status, evidenced by contract and payslips, in one exchange. You need to have held a full-time job at some point in the last 12 months. Beyond that there is no minimum, and a short history costs you nothing here. Misrepresenting the history you do have is disqualifying. Tell us the true version and you will not be penalised for it.

How the process works, and we tell you all of it now

  1. Application with a short Loom video. Research us first.
  2. A short test by email: one real decision task, your internet speed, your computer, and a paragraph on your work history.
  3. A 15 minute call with the founder.
  4. A recorded video interview. One take, no re-records. We verify the work history you've told us about.
  5. Aptitude tests. These inform us, they do not decide.
  6. A paid trial of six to eight weeks doing the real job.

The trial is where the decision actually gets made, including which of the two areas you end up owning. From the first week you will be making calls on live work, and we will tell you straight how each one landed. It is paid from day one: half rate for the first two weeks while you find your feet, full rate from week three onward, and a completion payment when you finish the trial, whether or not we hire you. If we stop early, you are paid for the days you worked.

Requirements

    1. Full time once hired, and this is your only job. During the paid trial you work 4 hours a day with us, 2 of them at a fixed time inside our working day, and you can keep your current job. If you pass, you give notice and join us full time within 30 days.
    2. Reliable internet, at least 30 Mbps down and 5 Mbps up, tested live with us.
    3. Strong written English.
    4. Based in Argentina.
    5. You track your working time with our time tracking tool from day one.

Benefits

2100 USD per month from day one, set by responsibility and demonstrated capability, not by how long you have worked.

On top of that:

  1. A one-month annual bonus.
  2. 15 days of paid leave a year, rising with tenure, plus your own country's public holidays.
  3. Paid sick leave.
  4. A health allowance.
  5. A coworking allowance.

Responsibility and pay move quickly here for people who earn them. Authority over decisions that reach a client moves slowly and deliberately, and it is earned on a track record rather than on a good first month. We would rather tell you that now than have you discover it in month two.

Why this role matters

Bitrise is where the world’s best mobile apps get built, tested and shipped. We’re the only mobile-focused company with an end-to-end platform that covers the whole release lifecycle. Now we’re growing from a product company into a platform company, and we lead with the value we bring to engineering teams: time saved, risk reduced and money well spent.

As a Head of Technical Success, you will help lead our team of Solutions Engineers (SEs) and Solutions Architects (SAs) serving as the trusted point of contact from a technical perspective for our customers. You will lead, mentor, and inspire a team of SEs and SAs to maximize customer retention, expansion, and long-term value. The SEs are responsible for owning the technical value in the pre-sales motion while the SAs own the technical adoption and value realization in the post-sales motion.

As the Head of Technical Success, you will own the technical playbook part of our Customer Journey map. The leader will help our customers create cutting-edge technical solutions that help them build better and more efficient apps.

Become a pivotal player in our Technical Success Team by:

  • Shaping the mobile tech landscape with your passion for solving complex challenges with elegant, scalable solutions.
  • Influencing the internal product roadmap
  • Mentoring your team, peers and others within the revenue organization and throughout the company
  • Owning and driving company impacting initiatives both internal and external
  • Engaging in thought leadership and be seen externally as an industry recognized expert in the Mobile and DevOps space

You will build and maintain important relationships with our customers - not just from the personal but from a technological side as well. Our customers are coming from diverse backgrounds, so you will have to rely on your deep technical knowledge, expertise and creativity when it comes to solving their requests. At the same time, collaboration doesn't stop there. Your role also includes bringing new development opportunities to our Product Teams. It also gives you a platform to share your experience and knowledge with a wider audience through various thought leadership activities such as blogs, webinars and conference talks.

Who you are

  • 10+ years experience in software development with ideally 3+ years as a leader/people manager
  • Expert-level experience with mobile app development or its processes
  • Experience in building rapport with VP of Engineering, CIOs and CTOs
  • You are familiar with publishing enterprise applications to the App/Play Store at scale

  • Advanced knowledge of regulatory landscapes across global markets
  • Expertise in emerging technologies and their impact on mobile development

  • Excellent problem-solving and communication skills

What you'll do

    • Collaborate with Bitrise product and engineering teams to provide feedback and industry trends to help shape the product roadmap.
    • Work with developers from our largest customers to debug complex Mobile DevOps issues, with a focus on CI/CD.
  • Stakeholder Management:
    • Act as technical escalation point for the global support team.
    • Be a thought leader for Bitrise in the marketplace, including attending and speaking at conferences, hosting webinars, writing blog posts.
    • Assist the Customer Success Managers to provide technical consultancy during the onboarding of enterprise customers.
    • Build deep relationships with technical champions within our customer base to enable them to become company advocates.

What we offer

jobs.excerpt: About the jobThe SOC Analyst is responsible for the continuous monitoring, triage, and investigation of security events across the organization's environment, as part of a global follow-the-sun Security Operations Center.
jobs.description:
About the job

The SOC Analyst is responsible for the continuous monitoring, triage, and investigation of security events across the organization's environment, as part of a global follow-the-sun Security Operations Center. This position reports to the SOC Lead. The role goes beyond acknowledging alerts: the focus is on understanding what each alert means, investigating suspicious activity end to end, responding to real threats, and handing over cleanly between regions so that nothing is lost across shifts. The ideal candidate has solid SOC experience, a strong investigative mindset, and thrives in a fast-paced, fully remote setting where accuracy, discipline, and security are essential. Hands-on engineering experience with core security platforms is a big plus.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor, triage, and analyze security alerts and events from the organization's security stack, including SIEM, Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), Security Service Edge (SSE), and Web Application Firewall (WAF) platforms.

  • Investigate security incidents end to end, from initial triage through analysis, containment, eradication, and post-incident documentation, coordinating with relevant teams throughout.

  • Determine the scope, severity, and impact of security events, separating true positives from false positives and escalating confirmed incidents according to defined procedures.

  • Execute response actions within the security platforms, such as isolating endpoints, blocking indicators, disabling compromised accounts, and enforcing access restrictions.

  • Ensure structured, high-quality shift handovers across regions in the follow-the-sun model, so that open investigations, ongoing incidents, and pending actions continue seamlessly around the clock.

  • Proactively threat hunt across endpoint, network, and log data to uncover suspicious activity that existing detections may have missed, mapping findings to frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK.

  • Provide feedback on detection quality and contribute to the tuning of SIEM correlation rules, EDR custom detections, and WAF rules to reduce noise and improve coverage.

  • Enrich investigations with threat intelligence, including indicators of compromise, attacker techniques, and emerging campaigns relevant to the organization.

  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, standard operating procedures, and incident response playbooks.

  • Collaborate with IT, infrastructure, application, and security engineering teams to resolve incidents and support day-to-day operations.

  • Support vulnerability management and drive continuous improvement of the organization's overall security posture.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

  • At least 3 years of hands-on experience as a SOC Analyst, triaging alerts and investigating security incidents in a production environment.

  • Solid working knowledge of core security technologies such as EDR, SSE, SIEM, and WAF, and of how to use them to investigate and respond to threats.

  • Hands-on experience implementing, configuring, and tuning these platforms, or writing and tuning detection content, is a big plus.

  • Experience with incident response and threat hunting, ideally with familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

  • Excellent understanding of network security, endpoint security, cloud security, and Zero Trust principles.

  • Relevant certifications such as Security+, CySA+, GCIA, GCIH, BTL1, or vendor-specific credentials are a plus.

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills with a high attention to detail.

  • Ability to handle sensitive information responsibly and securely.

  • Good written and verbal communication skills in English, and the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams and across time zones.

About You

You are a hands-on security analyst who wants to understand what is really happening behind an alert, rather than only closing tickets. You dig into the data, follow the evidence, and know when and how to escalate. If you have also stood up or tuned the tools you work with, or written your own detections, even better. You are structured, reliable, and comfortable working independently in a remote, follow-the-sun team, and you take pride in leaving a clear handover for the next shift. You are curious about new threats and technologies, and you enjoy working closely with both technical teams and end users to raise the security bar across the environment.

jobs.description:
About the Role

Osmind is an industry-leading interventional psychiatry group at the forefront of some of the most exciting advancements in mental health care, serving patients with some of the highest-acuity needs in behavioral health. None of that works if our customers aren't getting paid. When unpaid accounts receivable or cash flow problems arise, customers, our Customer Success Managers (CSMs), and our internal teams need a knowledgeable partner who can quickly explain what's happening, why, and what to do about it.

That partner is you. As our RCM Support Specialist, you'll be the first responder on revenue cycle tickets from our customers, the go-to revenue cycle expert for Customer Success and our internal revenue cycle teams, and a key support for our software-only RCM customers. Your focus is helping resolve unpaid A/R and protect cash flow across the full revenue cycle.

This is an internal support and advisory role, not a claims production role. You'll work across all accounts, supporting customers and colleagues wherever the need is greatest, and you'll be measured on the quality, clarity, and timeliness of the support you provide, not on claims worked or follow-up volume.

Osmind is a fast-growing startup, so processes are still being built and priorities change. If you like building structure as you go, there is real room to grow, including into a lead role as the team expands.

The ideal candidate combines two things that rarely show up together: deep revenue cycle expertise and a genuine strength in customer service, with polished written communication for customers and clear, concise verbal communication with internal teams. You're also someone who cares about the mission: you're passionate about revenue cycle, and just as passionate about helping behavioral health providers deliver care to the patients who need it most.

What You'll Do

    Help resolve unpaid A/R and protect cash flow

  • Own incoming revenue cycle tickets in our ticketing system, so the claims specialists working accounts don't have to
  • Investigate payment, denial, and billing questions across the full revenue cycle, from eligibility and prior authorization through claim submission, adjudication, payment, and A/R follow-up
  • Write clear, empathetic, customer-service-oriented responses that resolve the issue or set accurate expectations

    • Be the RCM subject matter expert for Customer Success

  • Serve as the direct resource for CSMs with questions on general revenue cycle topics, Osmind-specific processes, or specific claims
  • Help CSMs prepare for and navigate escalated customer situations with accurate context, recommended responses, and solutions
  • Answer broad healthcare and revenue cycle questions, including from colleagues and customers who are new to revenue cycle, drawing on industry trends and what you've seen firsthand working claims

    • Partner with our internal revenue cycle teams

  • Work alongside the staff who work claims, eligibility, and prior authorizations to understand trends, communicate findings, and close the loop
  • Translate what's happening on claims and prior authorizations into clear, concise explanations for Customer Success and other teams

    • Support our software-only RCM customers

  • Become an expert in Candid, our RCM platform, and use that knowledge to help software-only customers get the most out of it
  • Support customers with Candid setup and configuration, including rules engines, workflows, and account-level settings
  • Troubleshoot platform functionality questions and issues, and guide customers through features and best practices
  • Escalate platform bugs or configuration needs to the appropriate internal team with clear, concise context

    • Surface trends and drive product feedback

  • Identify patterns across tickets and escalations that point to product gaps, rule configuration opportunities, or process breakdowns
  • Communicate recommended changes clearly and concisely to our Product team on product enhancements, including what should change and why

What You'll Bring

    Required

  • Based in the United States. This is a US-based role, and applicants outside the US will not be considered
  • Behavioral health revenue cycle experience, or experience in a closely comparable specialty (for example, outpatient psychiatry or therapy practices, substance use treatment, intensive outpatient or partial hospitalization programs, neurology, infusion or physician-administered drug billing, or other specialties with heavy prior authorization and medical necessity requirements)
  • Deep, full-cycle revenue cycle knowledge, including eligibility and benefits verification, prior authorization, claim submission, payer adjudication, denials and appeals, payment posting, patient responsibility, and A/R follow-up
  • Hands-on experience working claims, so you can understand and explain what is happening on them
  • Strong knowledge of the broader U.S. healthcare landscape, including payer behavior and industry trends, and the ability to explain it to people new to revenue cycle
  • Demonstrated strength in customer service, with written responses that are warm, clear, and professional, and verbal communication with internal teams that is concise and confident
  • Strong investigative and analytical skills, including pulling and interpreting reports and performing root cause analysis on denials and payment issues
  • Demonstrated ability to get up to speed quickly on a new RCM system or healthcare service line, and then use that knowledge to support others independently
  • Ability to stay calm, constructive, and solution-oriented when stakeholders are frustrated
  • Comfort with technology, and a scrappy, adaptable approach to working in a fast-paced startup where processes are still being built, priorities change, and you figure things out as you go
  • Genuine commitment to Osmind's mission and to improving access to care for behavioral health patients

    • Nice to have

  • Experience with RCM or practice management platforms (e.g., Apero or similar)
  • Experience configuring rules engines or workflow automation in an RCM or practice management platform
  • Experience billing TMS, Spravato/esketamine, or ketamine-related services
  • Experience working in or alongside a customer success, support, or implementation team
  • Experience with ticketing systems (e.g., Pylon, Zendesk)

How You'll Work

  • Your two primary partners are Customer Success and our internal revenue cycle teams. You'll be the connective tissue between them, translating what's happening on claims into answers and solutions CSMs can act on.
  • You'll also work regularly with Implementation, Product, and other operational teams.
  • A team player. When a customer isn't getting paid, they're understandably upset, and that frustration often lands on CSMs. You'll approach these moments with empathy, curiosity, and a drive to help your colleagues solve the problem.
  • A clear communicator. You'll distill complex RCM findings into explanations that non-experts can act on.

Some candidates may see the list above and feel discouraged because they don't match all the items. Please apply anyway: there's a good chance you also have important skills we’ve missed! We are committed to diversity and building an equitable and inclusive environment for people of all backgrounds and experiences, and we're taking steps to meet that commitment. We especially encourage members of traditionally underrepresented communities to apply, including women, underrepresented people of color, LGBTQ+ people, veterans, and people with disabilities.

We are hiring a Senior Data Engineer to build and operate the pipelines, integrations and warehouse that support valuation and monitoring.

The platform currently captures change data from relational systems, processes it on Azure Databricks, and delivers it to Snowflake, Microsoft SQL Server and Databricks.   • Implement change data capture and incremental load, including ordering, deletes, replay and slowly changing dimensions.

  • Build medallion datasets and dimensional models, and deliver them to Snowflake, Microsoft SQL Server and Databricks.

  • Apply data contracts, reconciliation and row-level quarantine before publication.

  • Own the GitHub workflow and CI/CD, including tests, review, environment promotion and deployment as code.

  • Investigate production data failures, and turn requirements from product, valuation and client-facing teams into operable pipelines.

Requirements

  • 10+ years in data engineering on production systems.

  • Change data capture and event processing, including ordering, replay and schema change.

  • GitHub and CI/CD for data workloads, using GitHub Actions or an equivalent system.

  • Data quality, reconciliation, monitoring and production incident response.

  • Databricks Lakeflow, Auto CDC, Declarative Automation Bundles and DQX, or the Snowflake equivalents: Dynamic Tables, Streams and Tasks, Snowpark, Snowflake CLI deployments and Data Metric Functions.

Job Description

The U.S. Oncology business within our company is a growing and dynamic organization committed to advancing innovative therapies for patients with cancer. We have an exciting opportunity to join our dynamic commercial team as we prepare for the potential U.S. launch of an mRNA-based individualized neoantigen therapy for early-stage melanoma, being developed through an alliance partnership. This novel product has the potential to redefine personalized cancer treatment and requires a highly coordinated operating model to support seamless therapy delivery across a complex treatment ecosystem.

Reporting to the Director, Patient Support Strategy Lead, the Associate Director, Patient Navigator Strategy will serve as the business leader responsible for designing, building, and enabling the INT Patient Navigator capability within the INT Patient Support program. Given the complex nature of individualized neoantigen therapy and the coordination required across multiple stakeholders and treatment milestones, this role will establish the strategic framework for how Patient Navigators engage patients throughout the treatment journey, ensuring a consistent experience from enrollment through treatment completion. The individual will translate patient, provider, and operational insights into scalable capabilities, engagement models, and governance structures that enable effective patient interactions and operational excellence.

Key Responsibilities

  • Patient Navigator Strategy & Operating Model: Define the Patient Navigator strategy, operating model, service offerings, and engagement framework, establishing navigators as the primary point of contact for patients across the individualized therapy journey.
  • Patient Journey Support Strategy: Define how Patient Navigators support patients across key treatment milestones, providing education, guidance, and non-clinical support to help patients navigate a complex treatment journey.
  • Patient Education Strategy: Establish the strategy for patient education resources, including disease education, treatment journey expectations, manufacturing process information, anticipated timelines, and other non-clinical support materials
  • Patient Engagement Governance: Define consent-capture requirements, approved messaging, support guardrails, escalation pathways, and clinical versus non-clinical support boundaries across all patient-facing navigator interactions.
  • Technology, Data & Digital Enablement: Partner with Data & Technology teams to define technology requirements, CRM capabilities, workflow tools, reporting solutions, and patient visibility capabilities needed to support effective navigator engagement and service delivery.
  • Navigator Performance Management: Establish navigator performance measures, quality standards, service metrics, and reporting requirements. Leverage patient and operational insights to identify trends, barriers, and improvement opportunities that enhance patient experience and program effectiveness.
  • Cross-Functional Leadership & Program Optimization: Partner with Marketing, Patient Support Center of Excellence, End-to-End Therapy Operations, Legal, Privacy, Compliance, and other stakeholders to ensure compliant implementation, operational readiness, and continuous optimization of navigator capabilities.

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent (BA/BS)
  • MBA or equivalent preferred

Required Experience and Skills

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or healthcare organizations, with experience spanning patient services, patient navigation, patient support programs, care coordination, or related patient-facing functions.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and implementing patient support programs, patient navigation capabilities, or patient engagement models, with a track record of translating patient support strategies into operational programs
  • Experience establishing patient support guardrails, engagement standards, consent requirements, approved messaging, and operational processes that enable compliant patient-facing interactions.
  • Knowledge of patient privacy, informed consent, patient-facing communications, and compliance considerations related to patient support program design and execution
  • Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving capabilities, with a demonstrated ability to navigate ambiguity, resolve complex operational challenges, and translate strategy into execution.

Treasure AI:

Treasure AI is the agentic experience platform built to acquire, retain, and grow your most valuable customers. Powered by AI, Treasure AI is shaped by human creativity and always-on through continuous, context-driven action.

Furthermore, Treasure AI employees are enthusiastic, data-driven, and customer-obsessed. We are a team of drivers—self-starters who take initiative, anticipate needs, and proactively jump in to solve problems. Our actions reflect our values of honesty, reliability, openness, and humility.

Your Role:

Treasure AI is hiring a Security Engineer, GRC to architect, build, and automate the systems that power our Trust & Assurance (T&A) program. The right person for this role gets frustrated by manual compliance work — not because it's beneath them, but because they know it doesn't have to exist.

This role sits at the intersection of security engineering and GRC. You will design, operate, and maintain the systems that make compliance continuous, visible in real-time, and GRC insights actionable. You will treat the GRC platform as a programmable surface, extend it via APIs and agent workflows, and integrate it with the rest of Treasure AI's tech stack.

You will work closely with GRC Specialists, taking program requirements and translating them into technical implementations — automations, integrations, dashboards, guardrails, and tooling. You will also work directly with Security, IT, Engineering, and Product teams to embed compliance into the systems and pipelines they already use.

AI fluency is a baseline expectation. You will use agentic tools to accelerate your own work and will build AI-powered automations into GRC workflows — from evidence ingestion to questionnaire response to executive reporting.

Responsibilities & Duties:

  • Build AI agent workflows (using Claude, MCP integrations, or similar) to automate repeatable GRC tasks.

  • Configure and maintain the technical configuration and extension of our GRC platform — architect data relationships, configure control workflows, build custom rules, and extend the platform via APIs and webhooks rather than relying on the default UI.

  • Build automated executive readout workflows so monthly and quarterly GRC reporting is a 30-minute review, not a multi-day build.

  • Design and operate automated evidence collection pipelines and continuous control monitoring — pulling signals directly from source systems in real time so drift is surfaced before audit time, not during it.

  • Translate controls into testable, codified checks. Identify gaps in compliance coverage across CI/CD pipelines and IaC (Terraform) and contribute compliance logic where gaps exist.

  • Embed lightweight compliance checkpoints into design review workflows, ensuring control-relevant changes are flagged before deployment.

  • Support FAIR-informed quantitative risk modeling with data pipelines and tooling that make risk scenarios computable rather than narrative-only.

  • Build and maintain automation for the TPRM lifecycle — vendor intake, risk scoring, questionnaire distribution, evidence analysis, and remediation tracking — using AI-assisted tooling to reduce per-vendor manual effort.

  • Build tooling and dashboards that give the GRC Specialist and business stakeholders a continuous view of privileged access, access exceptions, and open remediation items — replacing point-intime UAR reports with an always-on IGA posture.

  • Build and maintain automation across the customer trust surface — AI-assisted questionnaire response pipelines, RFP contribution workflows, and trust center content management — so customer assurance accelerates deals rather than bottlenecking them.

  • Build automation across the security awareness and training lifecycle — detecting end-user risk signals or policy violations to improve the culture of security.

Required Qualifications:

  • At least 3+ years in Security Engineering, DevSecOps, Technical GRC, or a closely adjacent function — with a demonstrably strong engineering track record in automation and tooling, not just program ownership.

  • Strong coding foundation: proficient in Python and/or TypeScript, comfortable calling REST APIs, handling JSON/YAML payloads, building webhooks, and shipping integrations from scratch without hand-holding or assistance. You treat Jira, Confluence, Slack, and similar enterprise tools as systems to integrate with, not just UIs to click through.

  • Hands-on experience building automation and integrations in enterprise environments — not just configuring OOTB features, but writing code to extend or connect systems.

  • Practical hands-on experience with a modern GRC platform (Vanta, anecdotes, Drata, Secureframe, or similar) — you've configured custom workflows, written rules, and used the APIs; not just the UI.

About Reap

Reap is a global financial technology company headquartered in Hong Kong with employees across multiple countries. We enable financial connectivity and access for businesses worldwide by combining traditional finance with stablecoins for efficient money movement.

Through our stablecoin-powered corporate cards, payments, and expense management tools, we streamline financial operations and help businesses scale. Our APIs enable businesses to integrate stablecoin-enabled finance into their own products and services—from issuing Visa cards to facilitating cross-border payments.

Backed by leading investors including Index Ventures and HashKey Capital, Reap is building the future of borderless, stablecoin-enabled finance.

About the team

The Treasury team builds and operates the core infrastructure that moves money across our platform. We’re responsible for handling incoming and outgoing flows—fiat and stablecoins, internal transfers, withdrawals, and payouts. Our systems need to be reliable, observable, and audit-ready by default. We work closely with teams across the company to design systems that meet real-world operational, regulatory, and business needs.

What you’ll do

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will design and build global, asset-agnostic money movement systems that work seamlessly across regions, currencies, and financial partners. You’ll build flows that handle both fiat and stablecoins in production. You will partner with engineering, product, customer success, and finance teams to build systems with both internal and user-facing impact.

Responsibilities

  • Design and operate scalable systems that move and reconcile funds across jurisdictions, channels, and asset types

  • Build observability into every layer; lead incident response and drive long-term reliability improvements

  • Stay current with fintech, tech, and compliance trends, and evolve our systems accordingly

What we’re looking for

We encourage everyone to apply even if you just meet the minimum requirements. Preferred qualifications are a bonus.

Minimum requirements

  • Experience: Minimum of 6 years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning and operating business-critical systems (candidates with fewer years of experience may also be considered as Software Engineer).

  • Problem solving:You care deeply about correctness, edge cases, and failure modes. You approach problems methodically, debug with rigor, and prioritize clear, robust solutions over quick fixes.

  • Backend focus: You have experience working on backend systems and enjoy building APIs, services, and infrastructure that power real-world applications.

  • Data modeling and access: You’re comfortable working with relational databases like Postgres and MySQL, and have a solid understanding of transactions, data integrity, and performance tradeoffs. You’ve used ORMs like TypeORM or the equivalent in your stack, but know when to go beyond them.

  • Technical judgment: You balance technical depth with product understanding, and apply sound judgment when making tradeoffs. You build systems that are elegant under the hood, but practical and adaptable in real-world use.

  • Peer collaboration: You hold a high bar for code quality, reliability, and peer review, and value working closely with others who do the same. You communicate clearly, challenge ideas respectfully, and help raise the quality of the whole team.

  • Versatility: You’re comfortable learning new domains, working across the stack, and adapting quickly as priorities shift. You thrive in fast-moving environments and aren’t afraid to dive deep into unfamiliar systems.

  • Our main stack is TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, and AWS, but we value strong engineering fundamentals over any specific toolset.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Domain knowledge: Experience in financial domains—such as payments, disbursements, custody, or cards—is a strong plus, but not required.

  • Technical proficiency: You design systems that are stateless by default, built for scale, and resilient to failure. You’re comfortable with async workflows, distributed services, and cloud infrastructure.

  • AI fluency: You embrace using AI tools to accelerate development and explore ideas, but you apply them with discernment, not as a replacement. You know when to trust outputs and when to go deeper.

  • Full-stack experience:Experience across the stack (backend, frontend, infrastructure, data) is a bonus.

  • High-growth environments:Experience working in high-growth teams is a bonus.

jobs.excerpt: Peraton OverviewPeraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy.
jobs.description:
Peraton Overview

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Responsibilities

Job Description

Peraton is seeking a Director to lead the administration and user enablement of Peraton[x], our enterprise generative AI and agentic analytics platform. This leader is accountable for how the platform is configured, governed, and accessed, and for making sure every program that uses it can do so successfully. The Director leads a multidisciplinary team of system administrators, AI analysts, business analysts, and knowledge workers who onboard users, build reusable solutions, curate knowledge, and drive adoption across Peraton. The role connects end users, program leadership, and platform engineering. It turns business needs into well-administered platform capabilities and measurable adoption outcomes.

Job Responsibilities

Platform Administration & Governance

  • Lead all Peraton[x] system administration, including user and program provisioning, role-based access and data-tier management, environment configuration, and platform settings.
  • Set and enforce administrative standards, policies, and procedures for access requests, onboarding and offboarding, project and workspace management, and knowledge-base (cortex) governance.
  • Oversee release readiness and change management from the administrator and end-user side, including communicating platform changes, new features, and impacts to users.
  • Run the service desk and tiered user support model: ticket intake, triage, escalation to engineering, and resolution tracking against service-level targets.
  • Manage AI usage, cost, and license administration: track consumption and spend by program, attribute costs, and enforce usage policies.
  • Maintain administrative documentation, runbooks, and audit-ready records of access, configuration, and change.

User Enablement & Adoption

  • Own the Peraton[x] enablement strategy, including role-based onboarding, training curricula, office hours, user guides, and playbooks for new and experienced users.
  • Build and lead a community of practice and a power-user/champion network across programs to spread best practices and grow adoption.
  • Direct AI and business analysts in designing reusable skills, flows, workflows, dashboards, and templates that solve recurring program problems and lower the barrier to entry.
  • Partner with programs to identify high-value use cases, guide pilots, and scale successful solutions across the enterprise.
  • Measure adoption, engagement, and value using usage analytics and user feedback, and use the results to target training and improvements.

Knowledge Management

  • Lead knowledge workers in curating, organizing, and governing platform content, including enrolled documents, ontologies, knowledge graphs, and reference materials.
  • Set standards for content quality, metadata, classification, and lifecycle (review, archive, retire) so knowledge stays accurate and discoverable.
  • Maintain a central knowledge base of FAQs, how-to content, and lessons learned for users and administrators.

Team Leadership & Talent Development

  • Lead, mentor, and grow a cross-functional team of system administrators, AI analysts, business analysts, and knowledge workers.
  • Define roles, career paths, performance goals, and development plans, including AI literacy, prompt and agent design, and platform administration skills.
  • Plan staffing and hiring, and assign team members to programs based on enablement and support demand.
  • Build a culture of service, accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for program leaders and business units on platform access, onboarding, support, and adoption.
  • Gather and prioritize user and program requirements and represent them to product and engineering teams.
  • Report adoption, user satisfaction, support performance, cost, and value metrics to senior leadership.
  • Manage the administration and enablement budget, vendor relationships, and licensing.

Security, Compliance & Responsible AI

  • Make sure platform administration complies with Peraton policy, the Acceptable Use Policy, and relevant frameworks (e.g., NIST 800-171, CMMC, FedRAMP).
  • Enforce least-privilege access, data classification, periodic access reviews, and audit-evidence practices.
  • Promote responsible AI use through training, human-in-the-loop review, output verification, and governed approval workflows.

Qualifications

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, Education/Instructional Design, or a related field. A Master's degree is preferred.
  • 16+ years of experience in system or platform administration, IT service management, technology enablement, or analytics delivery, including 5+ years leading multidisciplinary teams.
  • Proven experience administering enterprise SaaS, collaboration, or analytics platforms, including user and access management, configuration, and governance.
  • Demonstrated success leading technology adoption, training, and change-management programs across large or distributed organizations.
  • Strong working knowledge of generative AI, LLMs, and agentic workflows, and how they create business and mission value.
  • Experience running service desk and user support operations (ITIL or equivalent).
  • Experience leading mixed technical and non-technical teams (e.g., administrators, analysts, knowledge managers).
  • Excellent communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to train users, brief executives, and turn technical topics into business terms.
  • Experience managing budgets, vendors, and licensing.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance, if required by the program.
  • U.S. Citizenship Required

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with knowledge management, content governance, ontologies, or knowledge graphs.
  • Background in instructional design, training development, or a customer success or enablement role.
  • Background in data analytics, business analysis, or all-source analysis.
  • Experience administering systems in regulated or DoD environments (NIST 800-171, CMMC, FedRAMP, ATO).
  • Certifications such as ITIL, Prosci/change management, PMP, AWS, or Agile/SAFe.
  • Experience with AI usage and cost governance (FinOps) and platform analytics.

Target Salary Range

Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.
